sentences.zh: 陳叔達陳叔達，字子聰，陳宣帝子也。

translations.literal: Chen Shuda—Chen Shuda, courtesy name Zicong, was a son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Shuda, whose courtesy name was Zicong, was a son of Emperor Xuan of Chen.

sentences.zh: 少封義陽王，歷丹楊尹、都官尚書。

translations.literal: In his youth he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yiyang and served successively as Intendant of Danyang and Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: While still young he was made Prince of Yiyang and later held the posts of intendant of Danyang and minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 入隋，久不試。

translations.literal: After Chen fell to the Sui, he long went without being given office.
translations.idiomatic: When the Chen fell to the Sui he went for a long time without receiving an appointment.

sentences.zh: 大業中，授內史舍人，出為絳郡通守。

translations.literal: In the Daye era he was appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and sent out as Administrator-General of Jiang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: During the Daye reign he was made a secretariat gentleman and then dispatched as prefect of Jiang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖西師，以郡聽命，授丞相府主簿，封漢東郡公。

translations.literal: When Gaozu marched west with his army, the commandery submitted on his orders; he was appointed Chief Clerk in the Chancellor's Office and enfeoffed as Duke of Handong Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu advanced west, the commandery submitted to him; Chen was named chief clerk in the chancellor's office and created Duke of Handong.

sentences.zh: 與溫大雅同管機秘，方禪代時，書冊誥詔，皆其筆也。

translations.literal: Together with Wen Daya he oversaw the secret archives; when the transfer of the mandate was imminent, all books, registers, and proclamations were in his hand.
translations.idiomatic: He and Wen Daya jointly managed confidential records, and as the dynastic transition drew near he drafted the books, registers, and proclamations.

sentences.zh: 武德初，授黃門侍郎，判納言，封江國公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude he was appointed Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, with concurrent duty as Head Censor, and enfeoffed as Duke of Jiang.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Wude he became vice minister of the palace secretariat, served concurrently as head censor, and was created Duke of Jiang.

sentences.zh: 叔達明辯，善為容，每占奏，縉紳屬目。

translations.literal: Shuda was bright and eloquent and skilled in deportment; whenever he presented memorials at court, the gentry fixed their eyes on him.
translations.idiomatic: Shuda was articulate and polished in manner; each time he spoke in council the officials focused on him.

sentences.zh: 江左士客長安，或汨滯，多薦諸朝。

translations.literal: Gentlemen from the lands south of the Yangtze lodged in Chang'an who were sometimes mired in obscurity were largely recommended by him to the court.
translations.idiomatic: Southerners resident in Chang'an who had fallen into neglect were often brought forward by him at court.

sentences.zh: 嘗賜食，得蒲萄，不舉，帝問之，對曰：「臣母病渴，求不能致，願歸奉之。」

translations.literal: Once, when food was bestowed on him, he received grapes but did not eat them; the Emperor asked why, and he replied, "My mother is ill with thirst; I could not obtain grapes for her and wish to take these home for her.
translations.idiomatic: Once when he was given food at court he received grapes but did not touch them. When the emperor asked why, he said, "My mother is ill with thirst. I could not find grapes for her and would like to bring these home.

sentences.zh: 帝流涕曰：「卿有母遺乎？」

translations.literal: The Emperor wept and said, "Do you still have a mother living?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wept and said, "Is your mother still alive?"

sentences.zh: 因賜之，又賚物百段。

translations.literal: Thereupon the Emperor granted them to him and moreover rewarded him with a hundred bolts of goods.
translations.idiomatic: He then gave him the grapes and also presented him with a hundred lengths of goods.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，與蕭瑀爭殿中，坐忿誶不恭，免官。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he quarreled with Xiao Yu in the hall and, on account of angry abuse showing disrespect, was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Zhenguan he quarreled with Xiao Yu in court and, for angry and disrespectful words, was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，居母喪，又有疾，太宗憂之，遣使禁卻吊者。

translations.literal: Before long he was in mourning for his mother and also fell ill; Taizong worried for him and sent messengers to forbid condolence visitors.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was mourning his mother and fell ill as well; Taizong was concerned and sent orders to turn away visitors offering condolences.

sentences.zh: 喪除，為遂州都督，病不拜。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he was made Military Governor of Suizhou but, being ill, did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: After the mourning period he was appointed military governor of Suizhou but, owing to illness, did not assume the post.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢禮部尚書。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was promoted to Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was promoted to minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 始，太子建成等鬩間太宗，帝惑之，叔達極意救辯，至是謂曰：「武德內難，卿有讜言，故以此報。」

translations.literal: Earlier, when the Crown Prince Jiancheng and others had sown discord against Taizong and the Emperor was swayed, Shuda had strenuously defended and argued on his behalf; now he said to him, "In the internal troubles of Wude you offered forthright counsel, and so I repay you thus.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Crown Prince Jiancheng and others had turned the emperor against Taizong, Shuda had spoken out strongly in Taizong's defense; now the emperor told him, "In the Wude succession crisis you gave me honest counsel, and this appointment is my reward.

sentences.zh: 叔達謝曰：「豈獨為陛下，乃社稷計耳。」

translations.literal: Shuda thanked him and said, "It was not for Your Majesty alone—it was for the sake of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Shuda thanked him and said, "I did not act for Your Majesty alone but for the realm itself."

sentences.zh: 後閨薄汗漫，為有司露劾，帝以名臣為護掩，授散秩歸第。

translations.literal: Later his conduct in the inner quarters was loose and unrestrained; the authorities exposed and impeached him, but the Emperor shielded this famous minister and gave him an honorary rank and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: Later his private conduct grew dissolute; the authorities impeached him, but the emperor protected this eminent minister, granted him an honorary rank, and let him retire to his estate.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰繆。

translations.literal: He died, and his posthumous title was Miu, meaning wayward.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was given the posthumous name Wayward.

sentences.zh: 久之，贈戶部尚書，更諡曰忠。

translations.literal: After some time he was posthumously made Minister of Revenue, and his title was changed to Zhong, meaning loyal.
translations.idiomatic: Some time later he was posthumously made minister of revenue and his posthumous name was changed to Loyal.

sentences.zh: 楊恭仁楊恭仁，隋觀王雄子也。

translations.literal: Yang Gongren—Yang Gongren was a son of Prince Guan of Sui, Yang Xiong.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Gongren was a son of Prince Guan of Sui, Yang Xiong.

sentences.zh: 仁壽中，累遷甘州刺史，臨事不苛細，徼人安之。

translations.literal: In the Renshou era he was promoted in stages to Governor of Ganzhou; in office he was not exacting in petty matters, and the people of the frontier were at ease under him.
translations.idiomatic: During Renshou he rose to governor of Ganzhou; he was not severe in small matters, and the frontier people lived peacefully under him.

sentences.zh: 文帝謂雄曰：「匪特朕得人，乃卿善教子矣。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wen said to Xiong, "It is not only that I have gained a good man—it is that you know how to teach your son.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen told Xiong, "I have gained a good man, but it is also you who have raised your son well.

sentences.zh: 大業初，轉吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Daye he was transferred to Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Daye he was made vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 楊玄感叛，詔率兵經略，與玄感戰破陵，敗之。

translations.literal: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, an edict ordered him to lead troops in pacification; he fought Xuangan at Poling and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Xuangan rebelled, he was ordered to take troops against him and defeated Xuangan at Poling.

sentences.zh: 遂與屈突通追獲賊。

translations.literal: He then pursued and captured the rebels together with Qu Tu Tong.
translations.idiomatic: He then joined Qu Tu Tong in pursuit and captured the rebels.

sentences.zh: 煬帝召見曰：「比聞與賊戰尤力，向但知卿奉法，而乃勇決如此，朕用自愧。」

translations.literal: Emperor Yang summoned him and said, "I have lately heard that in fighting the rebels you were especially strenuous; before I only knew you as law-abiding, yet you are so bold and resolute—I feel ashamed of myself.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Yang received him and said, "I have heard you fought the rebels with exceptional vigor. I knew you as a man who upheld the law, but I did not know you could be so bold—I am ashamed I underestimated you.

sentences.zh: 蘇威曰：「仁者必有勇，殆謂此邪。」

translations.literal: Su Wei said, "The benevolent must have courage—perhaps this is what is meant."
translations.idiomatic: Su Wei said, "The benevolent are always brave—this must be what the saying means."

sentences.zh: 時威及宇文述、裴蘊、裴矩參掌選事，皆受賕不法，恭仁素廉正，故惡之，出為河南道大使，使捕寇賊。

translations.literal: At that time Wei, Yuwen Shu, Pei Yun, and Pei Ju jointly managed selection affairs; all took bribes and acted unlawfully. Gongren had always been upright and incorrupt, so they disliked him and had him sent out as Commissioner of the Henan Circuit to capture bandits.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Su Wei, Yuwen Shu, Pei Yun, and Pei Ju controlled appointments and all took bribes. Gongren had long been upright, so they disliked him and sent him out as commissioner of the Henan circuit to hunt bandits.

sentences.zh: 至譙郡，為硃粲所敗，奔江都。

translations.literal: When he reached Qiao Commandery he was defeated by Zhu Can and fled to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: At Qiao Commandery he was defeated by Zhu Can and fled to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆，署吏部尚書，為化及守魏縣。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he was appointed Minister of Personnel and garrisoned Wei County for Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Gongren was made minister of personnel and left to hold Wei County for him.

sentences.zh: 元寶藏執送京師，高祖素知之，授黃門侍郎，封觀國公。

translations.literal: Yuan Baocang seized and sent him to the capital; Gaozu had long known him and appointed him Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat and enfeoffed him as Duke of Guan.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Baocang seized him and sent him to the capital. Gaozu already knew him, made him vice minister of the palace secretariat, and created him Duke of Guan.

sentences.zh: 尋為涼州總管。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he became Military Governor of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made military governor of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 恭仁久乘邊，習種落情偽，悉心綏慰，由蔥嶺以東，皆奉貢贄。

translations.literal: Gongren had long served on the frontier and was versed in the true and false ways of the tribal peoples; he devoted himself to pacification and comfort, and from the Cong Mountains eastward all presented tribute and gifts.
translations.idiomatic: Having long served on the frontier, Gongren understood the tribes well; he devoted himself to winning them over, and from the Pamirs eastward all sent tribute.

sentences.zh: 就加納言。

translations.literal: He was thereupon additionally made Head Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was also made head censor.

sentences.zh: 突厥頡利率眾數萬獵其境，恭仁應機設拒，張疑屯虛幟示之，頡利懼而走。

translations.literal: The Türk qaghan Jieli led several tens of thousands to hunt within his territory; Gongren responded opportunely with defenses, spreading doubt by encamping empty banners to show him, and Jieli, afraid, fled.
translations.idiomatic: The Türk qaghan Jieli led tens of thousands on a hunt into his territory. Gongren met him with a ruse, setting up empty camps with banners to deceive him, and Jieli fled in fear.

sentences.zh: 瓜州刺史賀拔行威叛，朝廷未即討。

translations.literal: He Ba Xingwei, Governor of Guazhou, rebelled, and the court did not immediately punish him.
translations.idiomatic: He Ba Xingwei, governor of Guazhou, rebelled, and the court did not move against him at once.

sentences.zh: 恭仁募趫蕩，倍道進，賊不虞其來，遂克二城。

translations.literal: Gongren recruited swift and hardy men and advanced by forced marches; the rebels did not expect his arrival and he thereupon took two cities.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren raised swift troops and marched at double speed; the rebels did not expect him and he took two cities.

sentences.zh: 縱所俘還之，眾感悅，遂相與縛行威降。

translations.literal: He released the captives and sent them back; the people were moved and pleased, and together they bound Xingwei and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: He released his prisoners, winning the people's goodwill; they then bound Xingwei and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 召拜吏部尚書，兼中書令，檢校涼州諸軍事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Personnel, with concurrent appointment as Grand Counselor, and was made Inspector of military affairs in Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as minister of personnel and grand counselor, with oversight of military affairs in Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 遷左衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was transferred to General-in-Chief of the Left Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was made general-in-chief of the Left Guard.

sentences.zh: 武德末，拜雍州牧、揚州大都督府長史。

translations.literal: At the end of Wude he was appointed Governor of Yongzhou and Chief Administrator of the Yangzhou Grand Protectorate.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Wude he became governor of Yongzhou and chief administrator of the Yangzhou grand protectorate.

sentences.zh: 遷洛州都督。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Military Governor of Luozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to military governor of Luozhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗勞謂曰：「洛陽要重，朕子弟不為少，恐非所任，故以委公。」

translations.literal: Taizong comforted him and said, "Luoyang is vital and important; I have no lack of sons and younger brothers, yet I fear they are not equal to the task, and so I entrust it to you.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong encouraged him and said, "Luoyang is critically important. I have many sons and brothers, but I fear none is fit for the post, so I entrust it to you.

translations.literal: (He concluded his remark.)
translations.idiomatic: (Thus ended the emperor's words.)

sentences.zh: 恭仁性沖厚，以禮自閑衛，未嘗與物忤，時人方漢石慶。

translations.literal: Gongren's nature was mild and substantial; he restrained himself with ritual in the guard service and never clashed with others; men of the time compared him to Shi Qing of Han.
translations.idiomatic: Gongren was mild and steady, disciplined himself with propriety in the guard, and never gave offense; contemporaries likened him to Shi Qing of Han.

sentences.zh: 既貴，不以勢尚人，故譽望益重。

translations.literal: Once he was eminent, he did not lord his power over others, and so his reputation and standing grew ever weightier.
translations.idiomatic: Once elevated he did not throw his weight around, and his reputation only grew.

sentences.zh: 病，乞骸骨，詔以特進歸第。

translations.literal: When ill he asked to retire; an edict granted him Special Advance and sent him home.
translations.idiomatic: When he fell ill he asked to retire; the emperor granted him honorary rank and let him return home.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈潭州都督，陪葬昭陵，諡曰孝。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Military Governor of Tanzhou, buried with honor at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous title Xiao, meaning filial.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made military governor of Tanzhou, buried at Zhaoling, and given the posthumous name Filial.

sentences.zh: 子 思訓子思訓襲爵。

translations.literal: His son Sixun—Sixun inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: His son Sixun inherited the title.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，歷右屯衛將軍。

translations.literal: In the Xianqing era he served as General of the Right Encampment Guard.
translations.idiomatic: During Xianqing he served as a general of the Right Encampment Guard.

sentences.zh: 從高宗幸并州。

translations.literal: He accompanied Gaozong on a visit to Bingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied Emperor Gaozong on a visit to Bingzhou.

sentences.zh: 右衛大將軍慕容寶節夜邀思訓與謀亂，思訓不敢對。

translations.literal: Murong Baojie, General-in-Chief of the Right Guard, invited Sixun by night to plot rebellion; Sixun did not dare reply.
translations.idiomatic: Murong Baojie, general-in-chief of the Right Guard, invited Sixun one night to plot a revolt; Sixun did not dare answer.

sentences.zh: 寶節懼，毒酒以進，思訓死。

translations.literal: Baojie, afraid, offered him poisoned wine, and Sixun died.
translations.idiomatic: Baojie, fearing exposure, gave him poisoned wine, and Sixun died.

sentences.zh: 妻訴之，流寶節嶺表，至龍門，追斬之。

translations.literal: His wife appealed; Baojie was exiled beyond the ranges, and at Longmen he was pursued and beheaded.
translations.idiomatic: His wife reported the crime; Baojie was exiled to the south, pursued to Longmen, and beheaded.

sentences.zh: 乃詔以寘毒人者重其法。

translations.literal: An edict was then issued to make the law heavier for those who poison others.
translations.idiomatic: An edict was then issued imposing heavier penalties for poisoning.

sentences.zh: 思訓孫睿交，尚長寧公主，豫誅張易之，賜實封五百戶。

translations.literal: Sixun's grandson Ruijiao married Princess Changning and took part in executing Zhang Yizhi; he was granted five hundred households of substantive fief.
translations.idiomatic: Sixun's grandson Ruijiao married Princess Changning, took part in killing Zhang Yizhi, and was granted a substantive fief of five hundred households.

sentences.zh: 神龍中為秘書監，貶絳州別駕。

translations.literal: In the Shenlong era he was Director of the Secretariat and was demoted to Vice-Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: During Shenlong he was director of the secretariat and was later demoted to vice-prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 弟 師道師道字景猷，恭仁弟。

translations.literal: His younger brother Shidao—Shidao, courtesy name Jingyou, was Gongren's younger brother.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Shidao, whose courtesy name was Jingyou, was Gongren's brother.

sentences.zh: 清警有才思。

translations.literal: He was refined, alert, and gifted in thought.
translations.idiomatic: He was refined, quick-witted, and talented.

sentences.zh: 客洛陽，為王世充所拘，間歸高祖，授上儀同，為備身左右。

translations.literal: He was a guest in Luoyang and was detained by Wang Shichong; he slipped away and returned to Gaozu, who appointed him Senior Companion of the First Rank and made him an attendant in the personal guard.
translations.idiomatic: While in Luoyang he was held by Wang Shichong but escaped to Gaozu, who made him a senior companion of the first rank and an attendant in the personal guard.

sentences.zh: 尚桂陽公主，除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: He married Princess Guiyang and was appointed Vice Minister of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He married Princess Guiyang and was appointed vice minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 改太常卿，封安德郡公。

translations.literal: He was changed to Minister of Ceremonies and enfeoffed as Duke of Ande Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of ceremonies and created Duke of Ande.

sentences.zh: 貞觀十年，拜侍中，參豫朝政，親遇隆渥。

translations.literal: In the tenth year of Zhenguan he was appointed Palace Attendant, took part in court governance, and received exceptionally generous personal favor.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year of Zhenguan he became palace attendant, joined in governing, and enjoyed the emperor's warmest favor.

sentences.zh: 性周謹，未嘗語禁省事。

translations.literal: His nature was thorough and cautious; he never spoke of confidential palace affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was thorough and cautious and never discussed confidential palace business.

sentences.zh: 嘗曰：「吾讀《孔光傳》，想其餘風，或庶幾云。」

translations.literal: He once said, "When I read the 'Biography of Kong Guang,' I think of the lingering style of his conduct—perhaps I may approach it somewhat.
translations.idiomatic: He once said, "Reading the 'Biography of Kong Guang,' I hope I may live up even in small measure to his example.

sentences.zh: 太宗數訪群臣才行，師道雖有所推進，而乏甄品。

translations.literal: Taizong often inquired into the ability and conduct of his ministers; Shidao, though he made some recommendations, lacked discernment in judging quality.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong often asked his ministers about talent and conduct. Shidao did recommend men, but he lacked the judgment to distinguish their merits.

sentences.zh: 久之，遷中書令。

translations.literal: After some time he was transferred to Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: After a time he was made grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 太子承乾得罪，詔與長孫無忌等雜治其獄。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince Chengqian fell into guilt, an edict ordered him, together with Zhangsun Wuji and others, jointly to try the case.
translations.idiomatic: When Crown Prince Chengqian was implicated in crime, he was ordered to join Zhangsun Wuji and others in investigating the case.

sentences.zh: 師道妻異姓子趙節與承乾通謀，乃微諷帝，欲活之。

translations.literal: Shidao's wife's son by a different surname, Zhao Jie, had conspired with Chengqian; he therefore subtly hinted to the Emperor, wishing to spare him.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao's stepson Zhao Jie had conspired with Chengqian, and Shidao subtly urged the emperor to spare the prince.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，罷為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and dismissed him to the post of Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and demoted him to minister of personnel.

sentences.zh: 師道起貴胄，四海人物，非所練悉，至銓署，專抑勢貴親黨以遠嫌，用人多違其才，不為時所稱。

translations.literal: Shidao sprang from a noble house and was not thoroughly acquainted with men throughout the realm; when it came to appointment and registration, he deliberately suppressed the powerful and noble and their kin to keep clear of suspicion, and in employing men often went against their talents, and was not praised by his contemporaries.
translations.idiomatic: Raised in the nobility, Shidao was not well acquainted with men throughout the realm. In appointments he deliberately held back the powerful and their kin to avoid suspicion, often placing men in posts unsuited to their talents, and won little praise.

sentences.zh: 帝亦曰：「師道資性純淑，自應無過，而實怯懦，罕更事，緩急不得其力。」

translations.literal: The Emperor also said, "Shidao's native endowment is pure and good and should be without fault, yet in truth he is timid and weak, rarely experienced in affairs, and in urgency or crisis cannot bring his strength to bear.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "Shidao's character is upright and should be blameless, yet he is timid, inexperienced, and useless in a crisis.

sentences.zh: 從征高麗，攝中書令。

translations.literal: He accompanied the campaign against Goguryeo as Acting Grand Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the campaign against Goguryeo as acting grand counselor.

sentences.zh: 軍還，頗不職，改工部尚書，復為太常卿。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was rather negligent in duty; he was changed to Minister of Works and again made Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: After the army returned he performed poorly and was made minister of works, then minister of ceremonies again.

sentences.zh: 師道善草隸，工詩，每與有名士燕集，歌詠自適。

translations.literal: Shidao was skilled in cursive and clerical script and adept at poetry; he often banqueted with famous scholars and sang and composed for his own pleasure.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao excelled at cursive and clerical script and at poetry; he often feasted with eminent scholars and composed verses for his own delight.

sentences.zh: 帝見其詩，為擿諷嗟賞。

translations.literal: The Emperor saw his poems, picked out lines of satire and allusion, and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read his poems, singled out lines of wit and allusion, and praised them warmly.

sentences.zh: 後賜宴，帝曰：「聞公每酣賞，捉筆賦詩，如宿構者，試為朕為之。」

translations.literal: Later, at a bestowed banquet, the Emperor said, "I hear that whenever you are tipsy and pleased you seize the brush and compose poetry as if prepared overnight—try composing one for me.
translations.idiomatic: At a later banquet the emperor said, "I hear that when you are merry you take up the brush and write verse as if it were already drafted. Compose one for me now.

sentences.zh: 師道再拜，少選輒成，無所竄定，一坐嗟伏。

translations.literal: Shidao bowed twice; in a short while it was finished, without any revision, and the whole assembly sighed in submission.
translations.idiomatic: Shidao bowed, and in a moment finished a poem without revising a word; the whole company marveled.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，諡曰懿，陪葬昭陵，詔為立碑。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously he was made Minister of Personnel and Military Governor of Bingzhou, given the posthumous title Yi, meaning exemplary, buried with honor at Zhaoling, and an edict ordered a stele erected for him.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of personnel and military governor of Bingzhou, given the posthumous name Exemplary, buried at Zhaoling, and granted a memorial stele.

sentences.zh: 子豫之，尚巢王元吉女壽春縣主。

translations.literal: His son Yuzhi married the Lady of Shouchun, daughter of Prince of Chao Yuanji.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuzhi married the Lady of Shouchun, daughter of Prince Yuanji of Chao.

sentences.zh: 居母喪，與永嘉公主亂，為主婿竇奉節所殺。

translations.literal: While in mourning for his mother he had illicit relations with Princess Yongjia and was killed by the princess's husband, Dou Fengjie.
translations.idiomatic: While mourning his mother he had an affair with Princess Yongjia and was killed by her husband, Dou Fengjie.

sentences.zh: 從孫 執柔執柔，恭仁從孫，歷地官尚書。

translations.literal: His collateral grandson Zhirou—Zhirou, Gongren's collateral grandson, served as Minister of the Department of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: His collateral grandson Zhirou, a collateral descendant of Gongren, served as minister of the Department of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 武后母，即恭仁叔父達之女。

translations.literal: The mother of Empress Wu was a daughter of Gongren's uncle Da.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Wu's mother was a daughter of Gongren's uncle Da.

sentences.zh: 及臨朝，武承嗣、攸寧相繼用事。

translations.literal: When she assumed the regency, Wu Chengsi and Youning succeeded one another in wielding power.
translations.idiomatic: When she took the throne, Wu Chengsi and Youning held power in turn.

sentences.zh: 后曰：「要欲我家及外氏常一人為宰相。」

translations.literal: The Empress said, "I want there always to be one person from my family and my mother's clan serving as Chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: The empress said, "I want our house and my mother's clan always to have one man as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 乃以執柔同中書門下三品。

translations.literal: She thereupon made Zhirou Associate Chancellor of the Secretariat and Chancellery of the Third Rank.
translations.idiomatic: She then made Zhirou associate chancellor of the third rank.

sentences.zh: 未幾，卒。

translations.literal: Before long he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died soon afterward.

sentences.zh: 弟執一，亦以誅張易之功封河東郡公，累官右金吾衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His younger brother Zhiyi also, on the merit of executing Zhang Yizhi, was enfeoffed as Duke of Hedong Commandery and rose in office to General-in-Chief of the Right Golden Crow Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Zhiyi, for his part in killing Zhang Yizhi, was created Duke of Hedong and rose to general-in-chief of the Right Golden Crow Guard.

sentences.zh: 始，雄在隋，以同姓貴；

translations.literal: At the beginning, Xiong in the Sui was honored for sharing the imperial surname;
translations.idiomatic: At first, in the Sui, Xiong was honored as a member of the imperial clan;

sentences.zh: 自武德後，恭仁兄弟名位益盛；

translations.literal: from Wude onward the brothers Gongren rose ever higher in fame and rank;
translations.idiomatic: from Wude onward the Gongren brothers grew ever more eminent;

sentences.zh: 又以武后外家尊寵，凡尚主者三人，女為王妃五人，贈皇后一人，三品以上者二十餘人。

translations.literal: and moreover, because of the honor and favor shown Empress Wu's mother's clan, there were in all three who married princesses, five daughters who became princesses consort, one posthumously made Empress, and more than twenty who reached the third rank and above.
translations.idiomatic: and with the empress's maternal kin honored, three men married princesses, five daughters became princesses consort, one woman was posthumously made empress, and more than twenty held rank of third grade or higher.

sentences.zh: 封倫封倫，字德彝，以字顯，觀州蓚人。

translations.literal: Feng Lun—Feng Lun, courtesy name Deyi, known by his courtesy name, was a native of Zhuo in Guanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun, known by his courtesy name Deyi, was a native of Zhuo in Guanzhou.

sentences.zh: 祖隆，北齊太子太保。

translations.literal: His grandfather Long was Grand Tutor to the Crown Prince of Northern Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Long was grand tutor to the crown prince of Northern Qi.

sentences.zh: 倫年方少，舅盧思道曰：「是兒識略過人，當自致卿相。」

translations.literal: When Lun was still young, his maternal uncle Lu Sidao said, "This boy's insight and strategy surpass others; he will reach minister and chancellor on his own.
translations.idiomatic: While Lun was still young, his uncle Lu Sidao said, "This boy's mind exceeds ordinary men's; he will rise to the highest offices on his own.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇末，江南亂，內史令楊素討之，署倫行軍記室。

translations.literal: At the end of Kaihuang in Sui the south of the Yangtze was in turmoil; Inner Secretariat Director Yang Su campaigned against it and appointed Lun Recorder of the Campaign Headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Late in Kaihuang the south rebelled; Yang Su campaigned there and appointed Lun recorder of his headquarters.

sentences.zh: 泊海上，素召計事，倫墜水，免，易衣以見，訖不言。

translations.literal: When they moored at sea, Su summoned him to discuss affairs; Lun fell into the water, escaped, changed clothes, and came to see him, and to the end said nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At anchor at sea, Su called him to counsel; Lun fell overboard, got out, changed clothes, and came to see him without mentioning it.

sentences.zh: 久乃素知，問故，謝曰：「私事也，所不敢白。」

translations.literal: Only after a long while did Su learn of it; he asked the reason, and Lun apologized and said, "It was a private matter and what I did not dare report.
translations.idiomatic: Only later did Su learn of it and ask why. Lun apologized and said, "It was a private matter and not something I dared report.

sentences.zh: 素異其為，以從妹妻之。

translations.literal: Su marveled at his conduct and gave him his cousin in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: Su admired his discretion and gave him his cousin in marriage.

sentences.zh: 素營仁壽宮，表為土工監，規構鴻侈。

translations.literal: Su undertook construction of Renshou Palace, memorialized to serve as Director of Earthworks, and planned a structure of vast extravagance.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Su built Renshou Palace, he petitioned to oversee earthworks and drew up plans on a scale of breathtaking opulence.

sentences.zh: 宮成，文帝怒曰：「素殫百姓力，為吾掊怨天下。」

translations.literal: When the palace was completed, Emperor Wen angrily said, "Su has exhausted the people's strength and incurred resentment throughout the realm on my behalf.
translations.idiomatic: Once the palace stood finished, Emperor Wen flew into a rage. "Su has drained the common people dry," he said, "and piled up the world's hatred upon me.

sentences.zh: 素大懼。

translations.literal: Su was greatly afraid.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su was seized with terror.

sentences.zh: 倫曰：「毋恐，皇后至，自當免。」

translations.literal: Lun said, "Do not fear; when the Empress arrives, you will naturally be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun said, "Have no fear. When the empress comes, you will be spared.

sentences.zh: 明日，帝果勞素曰：「公知吾夫婦老，無以自娛樂，而盛飾此宮邪？」

translations.literal: The next day, the Emperor indeed comforted Su, saying, "Sir, did you know that we husband and wife are old and have no way to amuse ourselves, and so you lavishly decorated this palace?
translations.idiomatic: The following day the emperor did exactly as Feng Lun had foreseen, praising Su: "You knew that my wife and I are old and have little to delight us—so you adorned this palace for us, did you not?"

sentences.zh: 因大悅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was greatly pleased.
translations.idiomatic: And with that he was well satisfied.

sentences.zh: 素退問：「何料而知？」

translations.literal: Su withdrew and asked, "How did you know beforehand?
translations.idiomatic: When Su withdrew, he asked, "How did you know?

sentences.zh: 倫曰：「上節儉，故始見必怒。

translations.literal: Lun said, "The sovereign is frugal by nature, so upon first seeing it he would surely be angry.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun replied, "His Majesty is frugal by nature, so his first reaction was bound to be anger.

sentences.zh: 然雅聽后言。

translations.literal: Yet he readily heeds the Empress's words.
translations.idiomatic: But he always listens readily to what the empress has to say.

sentences.zh: 后，婦人，惟侈麗是好。

translations.literal: The Empress, being a woman, loves only splendor and luxury.
translations.idiomatic: The empress, like any woman of her station, delights in nothing so much as magnificence and finery.

sentences.zh: 后悅，則帝安矣。」

translations.literal: If the Empress is pleased, then the Emperor will be at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Once the empress is pleased, the emperor will be content."

sentences.zh: 素曰：「吾不及也。」

translations.literal: Su said, "I cannot match you.
translations.idiomatic: Su said, "I am no match for you."

sentences.zh: 素負才勢，多所淩藉，惟於倫降禮賞接，或與論天下事，袞袞不倦，每撫其床曰：「封郎終當據此。」

translations.literal: Su, relying on his talent and power, often looked down upon and insulted others; only toward Lun did he lower himself with courtesy and generous treatment. Sometimes they would discuss affairs of the realm, talk flowing on without weariness. Each time he would stroke Lun's couch and say, "Master Feng will ultimately occupy this place.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Su, secure in his talent and influence, bullied and belittled many men; toward Feng Lun alone he showed courtesy and warm regard. They would sometimes debate affairs of empire until talk ran on without tiring, and Su would stroke Feng Lun's couch and say, "Master Feng, this seat will one day be yours."

sentences.zh: 薦之帝，擢內史舍人。

translations.literal: He recommended him to the Emperor, who promoted him to Inner Secretary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He recommended Feng Lun to the throne, and the emperor raised him to Inner Secretary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 虞世基得幸煬帝，然不悉吏事，處可失宜。

translations.literal: Yu Shiji gained favor with Emperor Yang, yet he was not well versed in administrative affairs and often handled matters inappropriately.
translations.idiomatic: Yu Shiji won Emperor Yang's favor, but he did not understand the business of government and often decided matters badly.

sentences.zh: 倫陰為裁畫，內以諂承主意，百官章奏若忤旨，則寢不聞；

translations.literal: Lun secretly made decisions for him. Inwardly, through flattery he carried out the Emperor's intent; if any official's memorial contravened the will, it would be shelved unheard.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun quietly made decisions in his stead. Within the palace he flattered the emperor's wishes into policy; any memorial from the officials that ran counter to the throne was left unheard.

sentences.zh: 外以峻文繩天下，有功當賞，輒抑不行。

translations.literal: Outwardly, he bound the realm with harsh laws; when merit deserved reward, he would suppress it and not carry it out.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he bound the empire in harsh law, and whenever merit deserved reward he blocked it from being granted.

sentences.zh: 由是世基之寵日隆，而隋政日壞矣。

translations.literal: From this Yu Shiji's favor daily grew, while Sui governance daily worsened.
translations.idiomatic: Thus Yu Shiji's favor rose day by day, and the governance of the Sui decayed with it.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及亂，持帝出宮，使倫數帝罪，帝曰：「卿，士人，何至是！」

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji raised rebellion, he took the Emperor out of the palace and had Lun enumerate the Emperor's crimes. The Emperor said, "You, a scholar—how could you come to this!
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, he led the emperor from the palace and ordered Feng Lun to recite the emperor's crimes. The emperor said, "You are a man of letters—how could you sink to this!

sentences.zh: 倫羞縮去。

translations.literal: Lun withdrew in shame.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun slunk away, burning with shame.

sentences.zh: 化及署為內史令，從至聊城，知化及敗，及結士及，得出護餉道。

translations.literal: Yuwen Huaji appointed him Inner Secretary Director. Following to Liaocheng, knowing Yuwen Huaji would be defeated, he then joined with Yuwen Shiji and was able to come out to guard the supply route.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Huaji made him Inner Secretary Director. Feng Lun followed him to Liaocheng, and seeing that Huaji was doomed, he joined Yuwen Shiji and managed to break out to protect the supply lines.

sentences.zh: 化及死，遂與士及來降。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji died, he then came to surrender with Yuwen Shiji.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji's death, he surrendered together with Yuwen Shiji.

sentences.zh: 高祖知其諧附逆党，方切讓，使就舍。

translations.literal: Emperor Gaozu knew he had ingratiated himself with the rebel faction and was just then sternly reproaching him when he sent him to his quarters.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozu knew he had curried favor with the rebels and was in the midst of sharply rebuking him when he ordered him to his lodging.

sentences.zh: 倫以秘策幹帝，帝悅，更拜內史舍人。

translations.literal: Lun presented secret stratagems to the Emperor; the Emperor was pleased and reappointed him Inner Secretary Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun offered the emperor secret plans; pleased, the emperor restored him as Inner Secretary Attendant.

sentences.zh: 遷侍郎兼內史令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Director and concurrently Inner Secretary Director.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Vice Director and given concurrent appointment as Inner Secretary Director.

sentences.zh: 秦王討王世充，命倫參謀軍事。

translations.literal: When Prince Qin campaigned against Wang Shichong, he ordered Lun to advise on military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin marched against Wang Shichong, he put Feng Lun on his staff as military adviser.

sentences.zh: 時兵久不決，帝欲班師，王遣倫西見帝曰：「賊地雖多，羈縻不相使，所用命者洛陽爾，計窮力屈，死在旦暮。

translations.literal: At the time the army had long been unable to achieve victory, and the Emperor wished to withdraw. The Prince sent Lun west to see the Emperor and say, "Though the rebels' territory is vast, they are loosely bound and cannot command one another; the one who receives their orders is Luoyang alone. Their plans are exhausted and their strength spent—death is imminent.
translations.idiomatic: The campaign had dragged on without decision, and the emperor wished to withdraw. The prince sent Feng Lun west to tell him, "The rebels hold much land, but their ties are loose and they cannot truly command one another; only Luoyang takes orders. Their schemes are spent and their strength broken—they are living from hour to hour.

sentences.zh: 今解而西，則賊勢磐結，後難以圖。」

translations.literal: If we disengage now and march west, the rebels' strength will become firmly knit, and later it will be hard to overcome them.
translations.idiomatic: If we pull back now, the enemy will knit their power together, and we shall never overcome them later.

sentences.zh: 帝納之。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted his counsel.

sentences.zh: 賊平，帝謂侍臣曰：「始議東討，時多沮解者，唯秦王謂必克，倫贊其行，雖張華葉策晉武，亦何以加於是！」

translations.literal: When the rebels were pacified, the Emperor said to his attending ministers, "When we first debated the eastern campaign, many discouraged it, but only Prince Qin said victory was certain, and Lun endorsed his plan—even Zhang Hua's counsel to Emperor Wu of Jin could not surpass this!
translations.idiomatic: After the rebels were crushed, the emperor told his ministers, "When we first debated the eastern campaign, most men tried to dissuade me; only the Prince of Qin insisted we would prevail, and Feng Lun backed him. Not even Zhang Hua's counsel to Emperor Wu of Jin could outshine that!

sentences.zh: 封平原縣公，判天策府司馬。

translations.literal: He was enfeoffed as Duke of Pingyuan County and made Acting Chief Administrator of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun was enfeoffed Duke of Pingyuan County and appointed acting chief administrator of the Heavenly Stratagem Office.

sentences.zh: 初，竇建德援洛，王將趣虎牢，倫與蕭瑀諫不可，至是入賀。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Dou Jiande came to aid Luoyang, the Prince was about to hurry to Hulao; Feng Lun and Xiao Yu remonstrated that it should not be done. At this point they came in to offer congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Dou Jiande marched to relieve Luoyang, the prince had meant to rush to Hulao; Feng Lun and Xiao Yu had urged against it. Now they came to offer their congratulations.

sentences.zh: 王笑曰：「不用公言，今日幸而捷，豈智者千慮或有失乎？」

translations.literal: The Prince smiled and said, "Had I not taken your advice, today I would fortunately have won—can even the wise, in a thousand considerations, sometimes err?
translations.idiomatic: The prince smiled and said, "Had I listened to you, I might never have won today. Even the wisest man, planning a thousand times, can still miss once, can he not?

sentences.zh: 倫謝素不及。

translations.literal: Lun apologized that he was not the equal of Su.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun apologized that he could not measure up to Yang Su.

sentences.zh: 頃之，突厥寇太原，且遣使和親。

translations.literal: Before long, the Turks raided Taiyuan and also sent envoys proposing a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward the Turks raided Taiyuan and at the same time sent envoys to propose a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 帝問計，群臣咸請許之可紓戰。

translations.literal: The Emperor asked for counsel; the ministers all urged accepting it to relieve the war pressure.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked his ministers for counsel, and all urged him to accept the offer and ease the fighting.

sentences.zh: 倫曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Lun said, "Not so.
translations.idiomatic: Feng Lun said, "That would be a mistake.

sentences.zh: 彼有輕中國心，謂我不能戰，若乘其怠擊之，勢必勝，勝而後和，威德兩全。

translations.literal: They harbor contempt for China, thinking we cannot fight. If we strike while they are slack, we are sure to win. After victory, then make peace—prestige and virtue both complete.
translations.idiomatic: They look down on the Middle Kingdom and think we dare not fight. Strike while they are careless and we are sure to win; make peace only after victory, and both authority and virtue will be intact.

sentences.zh: 今雖不戰，後必復來。

translations.literal: Even if we do not fight now, they will surely come again later.
translations.idiomatic: Even if we do not fight now, they will come again.

sentences.zh: 臣以為擊之便。」

translations.literal: Your subject holds that striking them is advantageous.
translations.idiomatic: Your servant believes it is better to attack them.

sentences.zh: 詔可。

translations.literal: An edict approved this.
translations.idiomatic: An edict approved his proposal.

sentences.zh: 尋檢校吏部尚書，進封趙國公，徙密國。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Acting Minister of the Ministry of Personnel, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and transferred to the state of Mi.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was made acting Minister of Personnel, raised to Duke of Zhao, and his fief was moved to the state of Mi.

sentences.zh: 太宗立，拜尚書右僕射，實封六百戶。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong ascended, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with a substantive fief of six hundred households.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong took the throne, he appointed Feng Lun Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs with a substantive fief of six hundred households.

sentences.zh: 始，倫之歸，蕭瑀數薦之。

translations.literal: At first, when Feng Lun returned, Xiao Yu repeatedly recommended him.
translations.idiomatic: When Feng Lun first came over, Xiao Yu had recommended him again and again.

sentences.zh: 及是，瑀為左僕射，每議事，倫初堅定，至帝前輒變易，由是有隙。

translations.literal: By this time Xiao Yu was Left Vice Director. Whenever they deliberated, Feng Lun would at first be firm in his view, but upon reaching the Emperor would change his position—thereby a rift arose between them.
translations.idiomatic: By then Xiao Yu was Left Vice Director. Whenever they deliberated, Feng Lun would hold firm in private, then shift his position before the emperor, and from this a breach opened between them.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年，遘疾，臥尚書省，帝親臨視，命尚輦送還第。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhenguan, he fell ill and lay abed in the Department of State Affairs. The Emperor personally visited him and ordered the Imperial Carriage Service to convey him back to his residence.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhenguan he fell ill and kept to his bed in the Department of State Affairs. The emperor came in person to see him and ordered the palace carriage service to take him home.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十，贈司空，諡曰明。

translations.literal: He died at age sixty, posthumously granted Grand Tutor, with the posthumous name Bright.
translations.idiomatic: He died at sixty, was posthumously made Grand Tutor, and received the posthumous name Bright.

sentences.zh: 倫資險佞內狹，數刺人主意，陰導而陽合之。

translations.literal: Feng Lun's nature was treacherous and sycophantic, narrow within; he often probed others' intent and secretly guided while openly agreeing.
translations.idiomatic: By nature Feng Lun was cunning and fawning, petty within; he constantly tested what others meant, steering them in secret while agreeing with them in the open.

sentences.zh: 外謹順，居處衣服陋素，而交宮府，賄贈狼藉。

translations.literal: Outwardly deferential and compliant, his dwelling and clothing were shabby and plain, yet in dealings with palace and government offices, bribes and gifts lay scattered in disorder.
translations.idiomatic: Outwardly he was meek and respectful, his home and dress plain and poor, yet in his dealings with palace and government offices bribes and gifts piled up in profusion.

sentences.zh: 然善矯飾，居之自如，人莫能探其膺肺。

translations.literal: Yet he was skilled at pretense, comporting himself at ease; no one could probe his innermost heart.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he wore his mask so easily that no one could pierce to what lay beneath.

sentences.zh: 隱、刺之亂，數進忠策，太宗以為誠，橫賜累萬。

translations.literal: During the disturbances of the Hidden Prince and the Assassination, he repeatedly offered loyal stratagems; Emperor Taizong thought him sincere and lavishly rewarded him with tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: During the troubles of the Hidden Prince and the Xuanwu Gate coup, he repeatedly offered loyal counsel; Emperor Taizong took him for sincere and showered him with rewards numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 又密言于高祖曰：「秦王恃功，頡頏太子下，若不早立，則亟圖之。」

translations.literal: He also secretly told Emperor Gaozu, "Prince Qin relies on his achievements and stands as an equal to the Crown Prince. If you do not establish him early, then quickly plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: He also secretly told Emperor Gaozu, "The Prince of Qin, trusting in his merit, stands shoulder to shoulder with the crown prince. If you do not establish him soon, move against him at once.

sentences.zh: 情白太子曰：「為四海不顧其親，乞羹者謂何？」

translations.literal: He secretly told the Crown Prince, "For the sake of the realm he neglects his kin—what shall one who begs for broth say?
translations.idiomatic: He secretly told the crown prince, "For all under heaven he forgets his own kin—what then shall a man who begs for broth say?"

sentences.zh: 及高祖議廢立，倫固諫止。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozu debated deposing and establishing heirs, Feng Lun firmly remonstrated to stop it.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozu debated removing and installing an heir, Feng Lun strongly remonstrated against it.

sentences.zh: 當時語秘無知者，卒後，事浸聞。

translations.literal: At the time these words were secret and none knew; after his death, the matter gradually became known.
translations.idiomatic: At the time these words were hidden and no one knew; only after his death did the truth slowly emerge.

sentences.zh: 十七年，治書侍御史唐臨追劾奸狀，帝下其議百官。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, Supervising Censor Tang Lin pursued investigation of his treacherous conduct; the Emperor submitted the matter for deliberation by all officials.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, Supervising Censor Tang Lin pressed charges of treachery against him, and the emperor referred the case to the whole bureaucracy for deliberation.

sentences.zh: 民部尚書唐儉等議：「倫寵極生前，而罪暴身後，所歷官不可盡奪，請還贈改諡，以懲憸壬。」

translations.literal: Minister of the Ministry of Revenue Tang Jian and others argued, "Feng Lun received the utmost favor in life, yet his crimes were exposed after death. His former offices cannot all be stripped; we request returning his posthumous grant and changing his posthumous name, to punish the crafty sycophant.
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Revenue Tang Jian and others argued, "Feng Lun was favored to the utmost while alive, yet his crimes were laid bare after death. Not every office he held can be revoked; we ask that his posthumous honors be withdrawn and his posthumous name changed, as punishment for a devious flatterer.

sentences.zh: 有詔奪司空，削食封，改諡為繆。

translations.literal: An edict stripped his Grand Tutor title, revoked his fief income, and changed his posthumous name to Erroneous.
translations.idiomatic: An edict stripped him of Grand Tutor, cut his fief income, and changed his posthumous name to Erroneous.

sentences.zh: 子言道，尚淮南長公主，官至宋州刺史。

translations.literal: His son Yan Dao married the Princess of Huainan, and rose to Prefect of Songzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yan Dao married the Princess of Huainan and rose to prefect of Songzhou.

sentences.zh: 裴矩裴矩，字弘大，絳州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Pei Ju—Pei Ju, styled Hongda, was a native of Wenxi in Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju, styled Hongda, came from Wenxi in Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 父訥之，為齊太子舍人。

translations.literal: His father Nezhi served as Attendant to the Crown Prince of Qi.
translations.idiomatic: His father Nezhi had been an attendant to the crown prince of Qi.

sentences.zh: 矩在乳而孤，及長好學，有文藻智數。

translations.literal: Ju was orphaned while still nursing; when grown he loved learning and possessed literary talent and strategic wit.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju lost his father while still at the breast; as he grew he loved study and showed both literary gift and shrewd intelligence.

sentences.zh: 再補高平王文學。

translations.literal: He twice served as Literary Companion to the Prince of Gaoping.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he served as literary companion to the Prince of Gaoping.

sentences.zh: 齊亡，不得調。

translations.literal: When Qi fell, he could not obtain an appointment.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi perished, he could obtain no post.

sentences.zh: 隋高祖為定州總管，召補記室，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: When Sui Gaozu was General-in-Chief of Dingzhou, he summoned him to serve as Recorder, but he left office due to mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When Sui Gaozu was general-in-chief at Dingzhou, he summoned Pei Ju as recorder, but Ju left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 高祖已受禪，遷給事郎，奏舍人事。

translations.literal: After Gaozu had received the abdication, he was transferred to Supervising Censor and attended to affairs of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: After Gaozu had taken the throne, he was made supervising censor and handled business for the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 帝伐陳，為元帥記室。

translations.literal: When the Emperor campaigned against Chen, he served as Recorder to the Commander-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor marched against Chen, he served as recorder on the commander's staff.

sentences.zh: 江左平，詔矩巡撫嶺南，未行，而高智慧等亂，道不通，帝難其遣，矩請速進，許之。

translations.literal: When the lands east of the Yangtze were pacified, an edict ordered Pei Ju to inspect and pacify Lingnan. Before he departed, Gao Zhihui and others rebelled and the roads were blocked. The Emperor hesitated to send him, but Pei Ju requested to advance quickly and was permitted.
translations.idiomatic: After the south of the Yangtze was pacified, an edict sent Pei Ju to pacify Lingnan. Before he set out, Gao Zhihui and others rebelled and the roads were cut; the emperor hesitated to dispatch him, but Ju asked to press on at once and was allowed.

sentences.zh: 次南康，得兵數千人。

translations.literal: Stopping at Nankang, he gathered several thousand troops.
translations.idiomatic: At Nankang he gathered several thousand soldiers.

sentences.zh: 是時，俚帥王仲宣逼廣州，遣別將圍東衡州，矩與將軍鹿願赴之。

translations.literal: At this time the Li chieftain Wang Zhongxuan pressed Guangzhou and sent a separate commander to besiege Dongheng Prefecture. Pei Ju went with General Lu Yuan to rescue it.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Li chieftain Wang Zhongxuan pressed Guangzhou and sent a subordinate general to besiege Dongheng Prefecture; Pei Ju marched with General Lu Yuan to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 賊立九壁，屯大庾嶺，矩進擊，破之。

translations.literal: The rebels erected nine fortifications and encamped at Dayu Ridge. Pei Ju advanced and attacked, breaking them.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels raised nine walled camps on Dayu Ridge; Pei Ju attacked and broke them.

sentences.zh: 賊懼，釋東衡州之圍，據願長嶺，又擊破之，斬其帥。

translations.literal: The rebels feared; they lifted the siege of Dongheng and took position at Yuanzhang Ridge. Pei Ju again attacked and broke them, beheading their commander.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels, alarmed, abandoned the siege of Dongheng and held Yuanzhang Ridge; Pei Ju struck again, routed them, and beheaded their leader.

sentences.zh: 自南海趣廣州，仲宣懼，潰去。

translations.literal: From Nanhai he hastened toward Guangzhou; Wang Zhongxuan feared and fled in rout.
translations.idiomatic: From Nanhai he pressed toward Guangzhou; Wang Zhongxuan, terrified, broke and fled.

sentences.zh: 綏集二十餘州，承制署渠帥為刺史、縣令。

translations.literal: He pacified and gathered more than twenty prefectures, and by imperial commission appointed local chieftains as prefects and magistrates.
translations.idiomatic: He pacified more than twenty prefectures and, by imperial commission, installed local chieftains as prefects and magistrates.

sentences.zh: 還報，帝大悅，詔升殿勞苦之。

translations.literal: Returning to report, the Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered him to ascend the hall to be praised for his labors.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned to report, the emperor was delighted and summoned him into the hall to praise his exertions.

sentences.zh: 拜開府，爵聞喜縣公，賜賚異等。

translations.literal: He was appointed to open an office, ennobled as Duke of Wenxi County, and granted extraordinary gifts.
translations.idiomatic: He was granted the privilege of opening his own office, ennobled Duke of Wenxi County, and given gifts of the highest order.

sentences.zh: 遷累內史侍郎。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Inner Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose by stages to Vice Director of the Inner Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時突厥強盛，都藍與突利構難，屢犯塞，詔太平公史萬歲為行軍總管，出定襄道，以矩為長史。

translations.literal: At the time the Turks were powerful; Dulan and Tuli were at odds and repeatedly raided the frontier. An edict appointed Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui as Campaign Commander to march out via the Dingxiang route, with Pei Ju as Chief Administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The Turks were then at their height; Dulan and Tuli were at odds and repeatedly raided the border. An edict made Duke of Taiping Shi Wansui campaign commander marching by the Dingxiang route, with Pei Ju as chief administrator.

sentences.zh: 破達頭可汗而萬歲誅，矩功不見錄。

translations.literal: They defeated Khagan Dadou, but Shi Wansui was executed and Pei Ju's achievements went unrecognized.
translations.idiomatic: They defeated Khagan Dadou, yet Shi Wansui was put to death and Pei Ju's merit went unrecorded.

sentences.zh: 還為尚書左丞，遷吏部侍郎，名稱職。

translations.literal: He returned to serve as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was transferred to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and his reputation matched his office.
translations.idiomatic: He returned as Left Assistant Director of the Department of State Affairs, was moved to Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and his name stood equal to his rank.

sentences.zh: 煬帝時，西域諸國悉至張掖交市，帝令矩護視。

translations.literal: During Emperor Yang's reign, all the states of the Western Regions came to Zhangye to trade; the Emperor ordered Pei Ju to oversee it.
translations.idiomatic: Under Emperor Yang, the western states all came to Zhangye to trade, and the emperor put Pei Ju in charge of the market.

sentences.zh: 矩知帝勤遠略，乃訪諸商胡國俗、山川險易，撰《西域圖記》三篇，合四十四國，凡裂三道：北道起伊吾，徑蒲類、鐵勒、突厥可汗廷，亂北流河至拂菻；

translations.literal: Ju knew the Emperor was eager for distant conquest, so he inquired of the merchant Hu about the customs of each state and the ease or difficulty of mountains and rivers, and compiled three fascicles of 'Records of the Western Regions,' covering forty-four states in all, divided into three routes: the northern route began at Yiwu, passed through Pulei, Tiele, the court of the Turk khagan, crossed the North-flowing River, and reached Fulin.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing the emperor hungered for distant empire, Pei Ju questioned the merchant envoys about each country's customs and the lay of mountains and rivers, and wrote three fascicles of 'Records of the Western Regions' covering forty-four states in three routes: the northern route ran from Yiwu through Pulei and Tiele to the Turk khagan's court, crossed the North-flowing River, and reached Fulin.

sentences.zh: 中道起高昌、焉耆、龜茲、疏勒，逾蔥嶺，鈸汗、蘇對沙那、康、曹、何、大小安、穆諸國，至波斯；

translations.literal: The middle route began at Gaochang, Yanqi, Kucha, and Shule, crossed the Onion Mountains, passed through Bohan, Suduishana, Kang, Cao, He, Greater and Lesser An, Mu, and other states, and reached Persia.
translations.idiomatic: The middle route started from Gaochang, Yanqi, Kucha, and Shule, crossed the Onion Mountains, passed Bohan, Suduishana, Kang, Cao, He, Greater and Lesser An, Mu, and the rest, and reached Persia.

sentences.zh: 南道起鄯善、於闐、硃俱波、喝般陀，亦度蔥嶺，涉護密、吐火羅、挹怛、忛延、漕國，至北婆羅門。

translations.literal: The southern route began at Shanshan, Khotan, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo, likewise crossed the Onion Mountains, passed through Humi, Tuhuoluo, Yandan, Fanyan, and Caoguo, and reached North Paropamisada.
translations.idiomatic: The southern route began at Shanshan, Khotan, Zhujubo, and Hepantuo, also crossed the Onion Mountains, passed Humi, Tuhuoluo, Yandan, Fanyan, and Caoguo, and reached North Paropamisada.

sentences.zh: 皆竟西海。

translations.literal: All reached the Western Sea.
translations.idiomatic: All three routes ended at the Western Sea.

sentences.zh: 諸國亦自有空道交通。

translations.literal: The various states also maintained their own routes through empty country for communication.
translations.idiomatic: The states also kept routes of their own through empty country by which they communicated.

sentences.zh: 既還，奏之。

translations.literal: Upon returning, he submitted his report.
translations.idiomatic: When he returned, he presented his report to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝引內矩，問西方事，矩盛言：「胡多瑰怪名寶，俗土著，易併吞。」

translations.literal: The Emperor summoned Pei Ju inward and asked about Western affairs. Pei Ju spoke at length: "The barbarians possess many rare and marvelous famous treasures; their customs favor settling the land—they are easy to annex.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor drew Pei Ju inside and questioned him about the west. Ju spoke at length: "The barbarians hold many strange and precious things; their people are sedentary by custom and can easily be swallowed up.

sentences.zh: 帝由是甘心四夷，委矩經略。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereby set his heart on the four barbarian directions and entrusted Pei Ju with frontier strategy.
translations.idiomatic: From this the emperor's heart turned to the four quarters, and he entrusted Pei Ju with frontier strategy.

sentences.zh: 再遷黃門侍郎，參豫朝政。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and participated in deliberations on court affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted again to Vice Director of the Yellow Gate and took part in deliberations on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 大業三年，帝有事恒山，西方來助祭者十餘國。

translations.literal: In the third year of Daye, the Emperor went to Mount Heng; more than ten Western states came to assist in the rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Daye the emperor performed rites at Mount Heng, and more than ten western states came to join the sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 矩遣人說高昌、伊吾等，啗以厚利，使入朝。

translations.literal: Pei Ju sent men to persuade Gaochang, Yiwu, and others, tempting them with rich profit to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: Pei Ju sent envoys to Gaochang, Yiwu, and the rest, baiting them with rich profit to come to court.

sentences.zh: 帝西巡燕支山，高昌等二十七國謁道左，皆使佩金玉，服錦罽，奏樂歌舞，令士女盛飾縱觀，亙數十里，示中國強富。

translations.literal: The Emperor toured west to Mount Yanzhi; Gaochang and twenty-seven other states waited by the roadside to pay homage. All were made to wear jade and gold ornaments and brocade robes, perform music and dance, and the emperor had men and women dress in splendor to watch freely, stretching for several tens of li, to display China's strength and wealth.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor toured west to Mount Yanzhi, envoys from Gaochang and twenty-seven other states lined the road to pay homage. They were decked in jade and gold, clad in brocade, and made to sing and dance while richly dressed men and women looked on for miles, a display of the Middle Kingdom's power and wealth.

sentences.zh: 後遂破吐谷渾，拓地數千里，遣兵出戍，歲委輸巨億萬計。

translations.literal: Afterwards they crushed Tuyuhun, extended territory by several thousand li, dispatched troops to garrison abroad, and annual tribute shipments amounted to tens of millions.
translations.idiomatic: Later they broke Tuyuhun, pushed the frontier out by thousands of li, sent troops to garrison distant lands, and each year poured out tribute and supplies numbering in the tens of millions.

sentences.zh: 帝謂矩有綏懷略，擢銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor considered Pei Ju to possess a strategy of pacification and recruitment, and promoted him to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor judged that Pei Ju had a gift for winning men and soothing the frontier, and raised him to Silver-Gleaming Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 帝在東都，矩以蠻夷朝貢踵至，諷帝悉召天下奇倡怪伎，大陳端門前，曳錦縠、珥金琲者十餘萬，百官都人列繒樓幔閣夾道，被服光麗。

translations.literal: When the Emperor was at the Eastern Capital, Pei Ju, as barbarian tribute missions arrived in succession, urged the Emperor to summon all the world's strange performers and marvelous acts and array them greatly before the Duan Gate. More than a hundred thousand persons trailed brocade and wore gold earrings; officials and townspeople lined the route with silk pavilions, curtained towers, and canopied galleries, their dress bright and splendid.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor was at the Eastern Capital, barbarian embassies kept arriving one after another; Pei Ju urged him to summon every strange performer and wondrous act in the realm and parade them before the Duan Gate. More than a hundred thousand people dragged brocade and hung gold at their ears; officials and townsfolk lined the road with silk pavilions and curtained towers, all in dazzling dress.

sentences.zh: 廛邸皆供帳，池酒林皪。

translations.literal: Market lodges all provided tents; there were pools of wine and forests of meat.
translations.idiomatic: Every inn and market stall put up tents; wine lay pooled and meat piled like forests.

sentences.zh: 譯長縱蠻夷與民貿易，所在令邀飲食，相娛樂。

translations.literal: Chief interpreters allowed barbarians to trade with the people; local officials everywhere invited them to feasts for mutual enjoyment.
translations.idiomatic: Head interpreters let the barbarians trade freely with the people, and local magistrates everywhere feasted them for mutual delight.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷嗟咨，謂中國為「仙晨帝所」。

translations.literal: The barbarians sighed in admiration, calling China "the celestial court of immortal dawn."
translations.idiomatic: The barbarians marveled and sighed, calling the Middle Kingdom "the court of the immortal dawn."

sentences.zh: 天子以為誠，謂宇文述、牛弘曰：「矩所建白，皆朕之志，要未發，矩輒先聞，非悉心奉國，疇能是邪？」

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven thought this sincere and said to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong, "The proposals Ju has put forward are all my own intent; before I had even voiced them, Ju would already have heard of them. Unless one serves the state with all one's heart, who could do such a thing?
translations.idiomatic: The Son of Heaven took this for truth and said to Yuwen Shu and Niu Hong, "Everything Pei Ju has proposed has been my own wish. Before I had even spoken, he was already ahead of me. Who but a man utterly devoted to the state could do that?

sentences.zh: 又助城伊吾，脅處羅入朝。

translations.literal: He also assisted in fortifying Yiwu and coerced Chuluo to come to court.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped strengthen Yiwu and forced Chuluo to submit and enter the Tang court.

sentences.zh: 帝益喜，賜貂裘、西胡珍器。

translations.literal: The Emperor grew still more pleased and bestowed a sable fur coat and precious vessels from the Western Hu.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor was increasingly delighted and rewarded him with a sable cloak and rare treasures from the western regions.

sentences.zh: 從帝巡塞北，幸啟民帳。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor on a tour of the northern frontier and visited Qimin Khan's tent.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the Emperor on a northern frontier tour and was received in Qimin Khan's camp.

sentences.zh: 時高麗遣使先在突厥，啟民引見帝。

translations.literal: At that time Goguryeo had already sent envoys who were with the Turks, and Qimin presented them to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Goguryeo's envoys were already lodged with the Turks, and Qimin brought them before the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 矩因奏言：「高麗本孤竹國，周以封箕子，漢分三郡，今乃不臣，先帝疾之，欲討久矣。

translations.literal: Ju thereupon memorialized, saying, 'Goguryeo was originally the state of Gushu; Zhou enfeoffed Jizi there, and Han divided it into three commanderies. Now it refuses to submit; the late Emperor resented this and long wished to chastise it.
translations.idiomatic: Ju then addressed the throne: 'Goguryeo began as the kingdom of Gushu. Zhou invested Jizi there; Han carved it into three commanderies. Yet it now withholds allegiance—a grievance the late Emperor nursed for years, always intending to punish it.

sentences.zh: 方陛下時，安得不事？

translations.literal: When Your Majesty was still heir, how could they fail to serve?
translations.idiomatic: While you were still crown prince, how could they have dared withhold obedience?

sentences.zh: 今其使朝突厥，及見啟民，舉國臣服，脅令入朝，可致也。

translations.literal: Now their envoys pay court to the Turks; when they see Qimin, the whole state will submit. Compel them to enter our court, and it can be achieved.
translations.idiomatic: Their ambassadors already kneel to the Turks. Once they behold Qimin and see the whole realm bow, we can pressure their king to come to court ourselves.

sentences.zh: 請面詔其使，令歸語王，有如旅拒，方率突厥誅之。」

translations.literal: I ask that Your Majesty issue the edict to their envoys in person and have them return to tell their king: if they refuse like travelers resisting, then I shall lead the Turks to punish them.
translations.idiomatic: Summon their envoys, speak the decree to their faces, and send them home with this warning: if their king balks, I will march with the Turks and destroy him.

sentences.zh: 帝納焉。

translations.literal: The Emperor accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor approved the plan.

sentences.zh: 高麗不聽命，征遼自此始。

translations.literal: Goguryeo did not obey, and the campaign against Liaodong began from this.
translations.idiomatic: When Goguryeo defied the order, the wars against Liaodong began.

sentences.zh: 王師再臨遼，皆從，以勞加右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the imperial army went twice to Liaodong, he followed both times; for his exertions he was promoted to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied both eastern expeditions against Liaodong and, for his service, was raised to Right Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 時綱紀汩振，宇文述、虞世基用事，官以賄遷，唯矩挺節無穢聲，世頗稱之。

translations.literal: At that time discipline was thrown into disorder; Yuwen Shu and Yu Shiqi held power, and offices were obtained through bribery. Only Ju upheld his integrity without tainted reputation, and the world spoke well of him.
translations.idiomatic: Law and order had collapsed. Yuwen Shu and Yu Shiqi ran the government, and posts changed hands through bribes. Ju alone kept his name clean, and people praised him for it.

sentences.zh: 矩以始畢可汗眾漸盛，建請以宗女嫁叱吉設，建為南面可汗，分其勢。

translations.literal: Ju, seeing that Khan Shibi's forces were gradually growing strong, proposed that an imperial clanswoman be married to Chijishe and that he be installed as Khan of the Southern Front to divide their power.
translations.idiomatic: As Shibi Khan's strength swelled, Ju urged marrying a princess of the imperial clan to Chijishe and making him Southern Khan to split Turkic power.

sentences.zh: 叱吉不敢受。

translations.literal: Chijishe did not dare accept.
translations.idiomatic: Chijishe refused to take the offer.

sentences.zh: 始畢聞之，稍怨望。

translations.literal: When Shibi heard of this, he harbored growing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: Shibi learned of the scheme and grew resentful.

sentences.zh: 矩又言：「突厥淳陋，易離間，但內多群胡教導之。

translations.literal: Ju also said, 'The Turks are crude and simple, easy to sow discord among—but within them many groups of Hu instruct and guide them.
translations.idiomatic: Ju added, 'The Turks are blunt and unsophisticated, easy to turn against one another—except that many Hu factions among them whisper counsel.

sentences.zh: 臣聞史蜀胡悉尤有謀，幸于始畢，請殺之。」

translations.literal: I have heard that Shi Shu Husiyou is especially crafty and favored by Shibi—I request that he be killed.
translations.idiomatic: I hear Shi Shu Husiyou is the cleverest of them and enjoys Shibi's trust. Execute him.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「善。」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, 'Good.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'Do it.'

sentences.zh: 矩因詭計召胡悉受賜，斬馬邑下，報始畢曰：「史蜀胡悉背可汗，我所共惡，今既誅之。」

translations.literal: Ju then used a ruse to summon Husiyou to receive gifts and beheaded him below Mayi, reporting to Shibi, 'Shi Shu Husiyou turned against the khan—we both detested him, and now he has been executed.'
translations.idiomatic: Ju lured Husiyou to Mayi with the promise of an imperial gift, then cut off his head and told Shibi, 'Husiyou betrayed you. We both hated him, so I killed him for us.'

sentences.zh: 始畢知狀，由是不朝。

translations.literal: When Shibi learned the truth, from then on he stopped coming to court.
translations.idiomatic: Once Shibi understood the trick, he never came to court again.

sentences.zh: 後帝北巡，始畢率騎十萬圍帝雁門，詔矩與虞世基宿朝堂待顧問。

translations.literal: Later the Emperor toured the north; Shibi led a hundred thousand horsemen to surround the Emperor at Yanmen. Ju and Yu Shiqi were ordered to remain overnight in the audience hall awaiting consultation.
translations.idiomatic: During a later northern tour, Shibi besieged the Emperor at Yanmen with a hundred thousand riders. Ju and Yu Shiqi were told to sleep in the hall and stand ready for counsel.

sentences.zh: 圍解，從幸江都宮。

translations.literal: When the siege was lifted, he followed the Emperor to the Jiangdu Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After the siege broke, he followed the court south to the Jiangdu Palace.

sentences.zh: 時盜賊蜂結，郡縣上奏不可計，矩言於帝。

translations.literal: At that time bandits swarmed like bees; the count of memorials from counties and prefectures was beyond reckoning—Ju spoke of this to the Emperor.
translations.idiomatic: Rebels were rising everywhere, and reports from the provinces piled up beyond counting. Ju laid the crisis before the Emperor.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，遣詣京師，以疾解。

translations.literal: The Emperor was angry and sent him to the capital, relieving him on grounds of illness.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor flew into a rage, recalled him to the capital, and dismissed him on the pretext of illness.

sentences.zh: 俄而高祖入關，帝令虞世基問方略，矩曰：「唯願陛下亟西，天下定矣。」

translations.literal: Before long Gaozu entered the Pass; the Emperor had Yu Shiqi ask about strategy, and Ju said, 'I only wish Your Majesty would hurry west—the realm will be settled.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Gaozu marched through the Pass. The Emperor asked Yu Shiqi for counsel, and Ju answered, 'Move west at once, and the empire will be yours.

translations.literal: (Close of quotation.)
translations.idiomatic: (Thus ended his counsel.)

sentences.zh: 矩性勤謹，未嘗忤物，見天下方亂，其待遇士尤厚，雖廝役皆得其歡。

translations.literal: Ju was by nature diligent and careful and never gave offense; seeing the realm was in turmoil, he treated scholars with particular generosity—even menial servants all found favor with him.
translations.idiomatic: Diligent and tactful by nature, Ju never crossed others. As chaos spread, he treated men of talent with exceptional kindness, winning even the affection of servants.

sentences.zh: 是時，衛兵數逃去，帝憂之，以問矩。

translations.literal: At that time palace guards frequently fled; the Emperor was worried and asked Ju about it.
translations.idiomatic: Palace guards were deserting in numbers, and the troubled Emperor turned to Ju.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「今乘輿淹狩已二年，諸驍果皆無家，人無匹合，則不久安，臣請皆聽納室。」

translations.literal: Ju said, 'The imperial carriage has tarried on tour for two years already; all the elite guards have no homes. When men have no wives, they cannot long remain content—I request that they all be permitted to take wives.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, 'Your Majesty has hunted away from home for two years. These crack troops have no families. Men without wives cannot stay loyal long. Let them marry.

sentences.zh: 帝笑曰：「公定多智。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, 'You are surely full of resourcefulness.'
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor laughed. 'You always know what men need.'

sentences.zh: 因詔矩盡召江都女子、孀家，恣將士所欲，即配之，人情翕然相悅，曰：「裴公惠也！」

translations.literal: Accordingly the Emperor ordered Ju to summon all the women and widows of Jiangdu, let the officers and soldiers take whomever they wished, and assign them at once. Sentiment turned harmonious and pleased, and they said, 'Lord Pei is generous!'
translations.idiomatic: He then had Ju gather Jiangdu's unmarried women and widows, let the soldiers choose freely, and paired them on the spot. Morale soared, and the men cried, 'Lord Pei has blessed us!'

sentences.zh: 宇文化及亂，眾劫矩。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji rebelled, the mob seized Ju.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuwen Huaji rose in revolt, the mutineers seized Ju.

sentences.zh: 賊皆曰：「裴黃門無豫也。」

translations.literal: The rebels all said, 'Vice Director Pei had no part in this.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels shouted, 'Vice Director Pei is innocent!

sentences.zh: 既而眾以秦王子浩為帝，詔矩為侍內，隨而北。

translations.literal: Thereupon the crowd enthroned Prince Hao of Qin as emperor and appointed Ju Palace Attendant; he followed them north.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels then set up Prince Hao of Qin as emperor, made Ju a palace attendant, and marched north with him.

sentences.zh: 化及僭位，署矩尚書右僕射，為河北道安撫大使。

translations.literal: When Huaji usurped the throne, he appointed Ju Right Vice Minister of the Department of State Affairs and Commissioner for Pacification of Hebei Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: After Huaji declared himself emperor, he named Ju Right Vice Minister of State and Commissioner for Pacifying Hebei.

sentences.zh: 又為竇建德所獲，建德以矩隋舊臣，遇之厚。

translations.literal: He was again captured by Dou Jiande, who, because Ju was a former Sui minister, treated him generously.
translations.idiomatic: Dou Jiande captured him next but, honoring him as a veteran Sui statesman, treated him well.

sentences.zh: 建德起群盜，非有君臣制度，矩為略制朝儀，不閱月，憲章擬王者，建德尊禮之。

translations.literal: Dou Jiande had risen from bandit ranks and had no system of monarch and subject; Ju drew up court ritual for him, and within less than a month regulations constituted in imitation of a king—Dou Jiande honored and respected him.
translations.idiomatic: Dou had risen from banditry and knew nothing of court order. Ju drafted rites for him; within a month his camp looked almost royal, and Dou treated him with deference.

sentences.zh: 建德敗，來朝，擢殿中侍御史，爵安邑縣公。

translations.literal: When Dou Jiande was defeated, Ju came to court and was promoted to Attendant Censor in the Hall of Governance, enfeoffed as Duke of Anyi County.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou's defeat Ju submitted to Tang, was made Attendant Censor, and received the title Duke of Anyi County.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子詹事、檢校侍中。

translations.literal: He was successively promoted to Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through the posts of Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent and Acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數盜邊，高祖遣使約西突厥連和，突厥因請婚。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly raided the frontier; Gaozu sent envoys to ally with the Western Turks, and the Turks thereupon requested a marriage alliance.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic raids battered the border. Gaozu sent envoys to court the Western Turks, and they asked for a marriage alliance.

sentences.zh: 帝曰：「彼勢與我絕，緩急不為用，奈何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor said, 'Their strength is far from ours; in crisis they would be of no use—what is to be done?
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor said, 'They are too distant and too weak to help us in an emergency. What then?

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「然北虜方熾，歲苦邊，若權順許，以示外援，須我完實更議之。」

translations.literal: Ju said, 'Yet the northern barbarians are at the height of their power and the frontier suffers year by year. If we provisionally grant their request to show external support, we may reconsider once we are strong and secure.'
translations.idiomatic: Ju replied, 'The northern enemy is strong and the border bleeds every year. Pretend to agree for now to show we have allies abroad, then decide again once we are secure.'

sentences.zh: 帝然其計。

translations.literal: The Emperor approved his plan.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor accepted the advice.

sentences.zh: 隱太子敗，餘黨保宮城不解。

translations.literal: When the Hidden Crown Prince was defeated, his remaining followers held the palace city and would not surrender.
translations.idiomatic: After the Hidden Crown Prince's fall, his partisans barricaded themselves in the palace and refused to yield.

sentences.zh: 秦王遣矩諭之，乃聽命。

translations.literal: The Prince of Qin sent Ju to instruct them, and then they obeyed.
translations.idiomatic: The Prince of Qin dispatched Ju to negotiate, and they finally submitted.

sentences.zh: 遷民部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of the Bureau of Population.
