translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Population.

sentences.zh: 太宗即位，疾貪吏，欲痛懲乂之，乃間遣人遺諸曹，一史受饋縑，帝怒，詔殺之。

translations.literal: When Taizong ascended the throne, he hated corrupt officials and wished to punish them severely; he secretly sent someone to present silk to various offices, and one clerk accepted the bribe-silk. The Emperor was angry and ordered his execution.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong despised graft and meant to crush it. He secretly sent silk to several offices as bait; one clerk took it. Enraged, the Emperor ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 矩曰：「吏受賕，死固宜。

translations.literal: Ju said, 'For an official to accept bribes, death is certainly appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Ju said, 'A corrupt clerk deserves death.

sentences.zh: 然陛下以計紿之，因即行法，所謂罔人以罪，非道之以德之誼。」

translations.literal: But Your Majesty tricked him with a stratagem and immediately applied the law—this is what is called entrapping a man with a crime; it is not the principle of guiding people through virtue.
translations.idiomatic: But you lured him into sin and then punished him. That is entrapment, not the way of teaching men through virtue.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，為群臣言之，曰：「矩遂能廷爭，不面從，物物若此，天下有不治哉？」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and said to the assembled ministers, 'Ju can truly remonstrate at court and not agree to one's face—if everyone were like this, would the realm not be well governed?'
translations.idiomatic: Taizong was pleased and told the court, 'Ju dares to argue with me in open session instead of nodding along. If every minister were like that, how could the realm fail to prosper?'

sentences.zh: 年八十，精明不忘，多識故事，見重于時。

translations.literal: At eighty years of age he was keen-minded and forgetful of nothing, knew much of precedent, and was highly regarded in his time.
translations.idiomatic: At eighty his mind remained sharp, his memory of precedent vast, and his reputation unmatched.

sentences.zh: 貞觀元年卒，贈絳州刺史，諡曰敬。

translations.literal: He died in the first year of Zhenguan, posthumously honored as Governor of Jiang Prefecture with the epithet Jing.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the first year of Zhenguan and was posthumously made Governor of Jiang Prefecture with the posthumous name Jing.

sentences.zh: 宇文士及宇文士及，字仁人，京兆長安人。

translations.literal: Yuwen Shiji—Yuwen Shiji, styled Renren, was a native of Chang'an in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yuwen Shiji, courtesy name Renren, came from Chang'an in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父述，為隋右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: His father Shu served as Grand General of the Right Guard of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His father Shu was Sui's Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 開皇末，以述勳封新城縣公。

translations.literal: At the end of the Kaihuang era, through his father's merit he was enfeoffed as Duke of Xincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of Kaihuang, he inherited his father's honors and was made Duke of Xincheng County.

sentences.zh: 文帝引入臥內，與語，奇之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen brought him into the inner sleeping chamber, conversed with him, and found him remarkable.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen received him in the inner chamber, spoke with him at length, and was impressed.

sentences.zh: 詔尚煬帝女南陽公主，為尚輦奉禦，從幸江都，以父喪免，起為鴻臚少卿。

translations.literal: He was ordered to marry Emperor Yang's daughter, the Princess of Nanyang, and served as Director of Imperial Transport Attendants; he followed the Emperor to Jiangdu, was dismissed on account of his father's mourning, then was reappointed Vice Minister of Reception.
translations.idiomatic: He was matched with Emperor Yang's daughter, the Princess of Nanyang, served as Director of Imperial Transport Attendants, followed the court to Jiangdu, left office to mourn his father, and later returned as Vice Minister of Reception.

sentences.zh: 其兄化及謀弑逆，以主婿忌之，弗告。

translations.literal: His elder brother Huaji plotted regicide; because Shiji was the emperor's son-in-law, Huaji distrusted him and did not tell him.
translations.idiomatic: His elder brother Huaji plotted regicide but, mistrusting the emperor's son-in-law, kept him in the dark.

sentences.zh: 已弑帝，乃封蜀王。

translations.literal: After the emperor was assassinated, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the assassination did Huaji enfeoff him as Prince of Shu.

sentences.zh: 初，士及為奉禦，而高祖任殿中少監，雅自款結。

translations.literal: Initially, when Shiji was an Attendant and Gaozu held the post of Vice Director of the Palace Administration, they voluntarily formed a warm friendship.
translations.idiomatic: Early on, while Shiji served as a palace attendant and Gaozu was Vice Director of the Palace Administration, the two had become close friends.

sentences.zh: 及從化及至黎陽，帝手書召之。

translations.literal: When he followed Huaji to Liyang, the Emperor sent a personal letter summoning him.
translations.idiomatic: When Shiji followed Huaji to Liyang, Gaozu wrote him a personal summons.

sentences.zh: 士及亦遣家童間道走長安，通諄勤，且獻金鐶。

translations.literal: Shiji also sent a household boy by a secret route to Chang'an to convey his earnest loyalty and present a gold bracelet.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji sent a servant by back roads to Chang'an with pledges of loyalty and a gold bracelet.

sentences.zh: 帝悅曰：「我嘗與士及共事，今以此獻，是將來矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and said, 'I once worked with Shiji; now with this gift he presents, he intends to come.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu was delighted. 'Shiji and I once served together. This gift means he is coming over.

sentences.zh: 化及兵日蹙，士及勸歸命，不從，乃與封倫詭求督餉。

translations.literal: Huaji's forces daily grew tight; Shiji urged submission but Huaji would not listen, so together with Feng Lun he falsely requested to supervise supplies.
translations.idiomatic: As Huaji's army collapsed, Shiji urged surrender in vain, then joined Feng Lun in asking to oversee supplies as a pretext to escape.

sentences.zh: 俄而化及敗，於是濟北豪傑謀起齊兵擊竇建德以收河北，觀形勢，士及不納，與倫等自歸。

translations.literal: Before long Huaji was defeated; thereupon the magnates of Jibei planned to raise Qi troops to strike Dou Jiande and recover Hebei. Reading the situation, Shiji did not assent and returned of his own accord with Lun and the others.
translations.idiomatic: Huaji fell soon after. Jibei's strongmen then proposed raising Qi forces to crush Dou Jiande and retake Hebei, but Shiji read the odds, refused, and surrendered with Feng Lun and the rest.

sentences.zh: 帝讓之曰：「汝兄弟率思歸之人為入關計，爾得時，我父子，尚肯相假乎？

translations.literal: The Emperor reproached him, saying, 'Your brothers led those eager to return home in plotting entry through the Pass—had you seized the moment, would I, father and son, even have spared you?
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu rebuked him: 'Your brothers marched homebound men toward the Pass to seize power. Had you timed it right, do you think my son and I would have spared you?

sentences.zh: 今欲何地自處？」

translations.literal: Where do you wish to place yourself now?
translations.idiomatic: Where do you imagine you belong now?

sentences.zh: 士及謝曰：「臣罪當死，但臣往在涿郡，嘗與陛下夜論世事，頃又奉所獻，冀以此贖罪。」

translations.literal: Shiji apologized, 'Your subject's crime deserves death, but when I was formerly in Zhuo Commandery I once discussed affairs of the age with Your Majesty through the night; recently I again presented my gift—hoping thereby to redeem my offense.'
translations.idiomatic: Shiji bowed low. 'I deserve death. Yet in Zhuo Commandery I once talked with you through the night about the fate of the realm, and I have just sent my gift in hope of atoning.'

sentences.zh: 帝笑謂裴寂曰：「彼與我論天下事，逮今六七年，公等皆在其後。」

translations.literal: The Emperor laughed and said to Pei Ji, 'He discussed the affairs of the realm with me nearly six or seven years ago—you all came after him.'
translations.idiomatic: Gaozu laughed and told Pei Ji, 'He and I debated the empire six or seven years ago—you all came later.'

sentences.zh: 時士及女弟為昭儀，有寵，由是見親禮，授上儀同。

translations.literal: At that time Shiji's younger sister was a Lady of Brilliant Composure with favor, and for this reason he received intimate honor and was granted Senior General of the Upper Class.
translations.idiomatic: His younger sister was then a favored palace lady, and through her favor he won close treatment and the rank of Senior General of the Upper Class.

sentences.zh: 從秦王平宋金剛，錄功，復隋舊封，以宗室女妻之，遷王府驃騎將軍。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Qin in pacifying Song Jingang; for his merit he recovered his old Sui enfeoffment, was given an imperial clanswoman in marriage, and was promoted to General of Swift Cavalry in the princely household.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the Prince of Qin against Song Jingang, recovered his old Sui title, married a princess of the imperial clan, and became the prince's General of Swift Cavalry.

sentences.zh: 從討王世充等，進爵郢國公。

translations.literal: He followed in the campaign against Wang Shichong and others and was advanced to Duke of the State of Ying.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Wang Shichong and was ennobled Duke of Ying.

sentences.zh: 武德八年，權檢校侍中，兼太子詹事。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Wude he served as Acting Palace Attendant and concurrently as Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of Wude he served as Acting Palace Attendant and Grand Mentor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 王即位，拜中書令，真食益州七百戶，以本官檢校涼州都督。

translations.literal: When the Prince ascended the throne, he was appointed Grand Counselor of the Department of State Affairs with a permanent fief of seven hundred households in Yizhou, and by virtue of his existing office served as Acting Regional Commander of Liangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Qin became emperor, he made Shiji Grand Counselor, granted him seven hundred households in Yizhou, and kept him as Acting Regional Commander of Liangzhou.

sentences.zh: 時突厥數入寇，士及欲立威以鎮耀邊鄙，每出入，盛陳兵衛，又痛折節下士。

translations.literal: At that time the Turks repeatedly invaded; Shiji wished to establish authority to overawe the frontier regions—whenever he went out or in he displayed troops and guards in grandeur, yet he also greatly humbled himself and treated subordinates well.
translations.idiomatic: Turkic raids were constant. Shiji wanted to awe the frontier, so he traveled with ostentatious guards yet humbled himself sharply before his staff.

sentences.zh: 或告其反，訊無狀，召為殿中監，以疾改蒲州刺史。

translations.literal: Someone reported him for rebellion; investigation found no basis; he was summoned as Director of the Palace Administration but due to illness was transferred to Prefect of Puzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Accused of treason, he was cleared on investigation, recalled as Director of the Palace Administration, then moved to Prefect of Puzhou because of illness.

sentences.zh: 政尚寬簡，人皆宜之。

translations.literal: His administration favored leniency and simplicity, and the people all found it agreeable.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was easy and plain, and the people approved.

sentences.zh: 擢右衛大將軍。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Grand General of the Right Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗延入閤語，或至夜分出，遇休沐，往往馳召。

translations.literal: Taizong would summon him into the privy chamber to talk, sometimes until the night watch ended; when there were rest days, he would often send urgent summons.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong would pull him into the inner chambers for talk that sometimes ran past midnight, summoning him even on days of rest.

sentences.zh: 士及益自謹，其妻嘗問遽召何所事，士及卒不對。

translations.literal: Shiji became all the more cautious; his wife once asked what urgent business the summons concerned, and Shiji never answered.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji grew still more guarded. When his wife asked why the sudden summons, he would not say.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗玩禁中樹曰：「此嘉木也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor once admired a tree in the palace precincts and said, 'What a fine tree!
translations.idiomatic: Once, admiring a tree in the palace grounds, the Emperor exclaimed, 'What splendid timber!

sentences.zh: 士及從旁美歎。

translations.literal: Shiji from the side praised and sighed in admiration.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji murmured praise at his elbow.

sentences.zh: 帝正色曰：「魏征常勸我遠佞人，不識佞人為誰，乃今信然。」

translations.literal: The Emperor's face hardened and he said, 'Wei Zheng often urged me to keep flatterers at a distance—I did not know who the flatterer was, but now I truly believe it.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's expression darkened. 'Wei Zheng keeps telling me to banish flatterers. I never knew who he meant—until now.

sentences.zh: 謝曰：「南衙群臣面折廷爭，陛下不得舉手。

translations.literal: He apologized, 'The ministers of the southern offices remonstrate face to face in court debate—Your Majesty cannot raise a hand against them.
translations.idiomatic: Shiji apologized. 'Ministers in the outer court argue with you openly, and you cannot simply brush them aside.

sentences.zh: 今臣幸在左右，不少有將順，雖貴為天子，亦何聊？」

translations.literal: Now your subject is fortunate to be at Your Majesty's side—if I did not somewhat accommodate, even though exalted as Son of Heaven, what pleasure would there be?'
translations.idiomatic: But I stand at your side. If I never agreed with you, even an emperor would find his days unbearably lonely.'

sentences.zh: 帝意解。

translations.literal: The Emperor's mood eased.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong's anger cooled.

sentences.zh: 又嘗割肉，以餅拭手，帝屢目，陽若不省，徐啗之。

translations.literal: On another occasion he cut meat and wiped his hands with a flatbread; the Emperor looked repeatedly, but Shiji feigned not to notice and slowly ate it.
translations.idiomatic: Another time he wiped greasy hands on a cake while the Emperor stared; Shiji pretended not to see and ate the cake anyway.

sentences.zh: 其機悟率類此。

translations.literal: His quick wit was generally of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His cleverness usually took that form.

sentences.zh: 後以雅舊，別封一子新城縣公。

translations.literal: Later, on account of their old friendship, one of his sons was separately enfeoffed as Duke of Xincheng County.
translations.idiomatic: Later, honoring their old bond, Taizong separately enfeoffed one of Shiji's sons as Duke of Xincheng County.

sentences.zh: 久之，復為殿中監。

translations.literal: After a long while he again served as Director of the Palace Administration.
translations.idiomatic: Years afterward he returned as Director of the Palace Administration.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈左衛大將軍、涼州都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously honored as Grand General of the Left Guard and Regional Commander of Liangzhou, and buried near Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made Grand General of the Left Guard and Regional Commander of Liangzhou, with burial near Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 士及撫幼弟、孤兄子，以友睦稱。

translations.literal: Shiji raised his younger brothers and his elder brother's orphaned sons, and was known for fraternal harmony.
translations.idiomatic: He cared for younger brothers and his brother's orphaned sons and was praised for family devotion.

sentences.zh: 好周恤親戚故人，然過自奉養，服玩食飲必極豐侈。

translations.literal: He liked to generously aid relatives and old friends, yet he excessively indulged himself—clothing, curios, food, and drink were always extremely lavish.
translations.idiomatic: He was generous to kin and old friends, yet spent extravagantly on his own comforts, food, and finery.

sentences.zh: 有司諡曰恭，黃門侍郎劉洎曰：「士及居家侈肆，不可謂恭。」

translations.literal: The relevant office proposed the epithet Gong; Vice Director Liu Ji said, 'Shiji was extravagant at home—it cannot be called respectful.
translations.idiomatic: The court first proposed the posthumous name Gong, but Vice Director Liu Ji objected: 'A man so lavish in private life cannot be called respectful.

sentences.zh: 乃改曰縱。

translations.literal: So it was changed to Zong.
translations.idiomatic: They changed it to Zong instead.

sentences.zh: 贊曰：封倫、裴矩，其奸足以亡隋，其知反以佐唐，何哉？

translations.literal: The appraisal says: Feng Lun and Pei Ju—their wickedness was enough to destroy Sui, yet their knowledge in turn helped Tang—how is this?
translations.idiomatic: The historian comments: Feng Lun and Pei Ju were wicked enough to ruin Sui, yet clever enough to serve Tang—how can that be?

sentences.zh: 惟奸人多才能，與時而成敗也。

translations.literal: Only the wicked often have great talent; success and failure accord with the times.
translations.idiomatic: Villains often possess great ability; fortune simply shifts with the age.

sentences.zh: 妖禽孽狐，當晝則伏自如，得夜乃為之祥。

translations.literal: Ominous birds and evil foxes hide at ease by day; only when night comes do they become portents.
translations.idiomatic: Evil birds and cursed foxes lie quiet by daylight; only in darkness do they pass for omens.

sentences.zh: 若倫偽行匿情，死乃暴聞，免兩觀之誅，幸矣。

translations.literal: As for Lun—he practiced false conduct and concealed his feelings; only after death were they exposed. To escape execution at the Two Gates was fortunate indeed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun wore virtue like a mask and hid his true heart until death exposed him. That he escaped execution at the Two Gates was luck enough.

sentences.zh: 太宗知士及之佞，為游言自解，亦不能斥。

translations.literal: Taizong knew Shiji was a flatterer; though Shiji pleaded excuse with clever talk, he still could not dismiss him.
translations.idiomatic: Taizong knew Shiji was a sycophant, yet even when Shiji talked his way out of trouble, the emperor could not bring himself to cast him off.

sentences.zh: 彼中材之主，求不惑於佞，難哉！

translations.literal: For a ruler of middling talent, to seek not to be deluded by flatterers—how difficult!
translations.idiomatic: Even a capable sovereign would struggle to keep flatterers from clouding his judgment—how much harder for one of merely average gifts!

sentences.zh: 鄭善果鄭善果，鄭州滎澤人。

translations.literal: Zheng Shangguo—Zheng Shangguo, a native of Yingze in Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Shangguo was a native of Yingze in Zheng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 祖在魏為顯家。

translations.literal: His grandfather was a prominent family in Wei.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather's house had been eminent in Wei.

sentences.zh: 父誠，周大將軍、開封縣公，討尉遲迥，戰死。

translations.literal: His father Cheng was a Grand General of Zhou and Duke of Kaifeng County; campaigning against Yuwen Jiong, he died in battle.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cheng, a Zhou grand general and duke of Kaifeng County, fell in battle while suppressing Yuwen Jiong.

sentences.zh: 善果方九歲，以死事子襲爵，家人為其幼，弗告也；

translations.literal: Shangguo was only nine; by the rule for sons of those who died in service he inherited the title, but the family, considering him young, did not tell him;
translations.idiomatic: Shangguo was only nine when, as the son of a man who had died on campaign, he inherited the title; his family, thinking him too young, kept the news from him;

sentences.zh: 及受詔，號哭不自勝。

translations.literal: When he received the edict, he wailed uncontrollably.
translations.idiomatic: When the decree finally reached him, he broke down in uncontrollable grief.

sentences.zh: 隋開皇初，進封武德郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaihuang in Sui, he was advanced to Duke of Wude Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Sui Kaihuang reign he was promoted to duke of Wude Commandery.

sentences.zh: 年十四，為沂州刺史。

translations.literal: At age fourteen, he became Prefect of Yizhou.
translations.idiomatic: At fourteen he was appointed prefect of Yizhou.

sentences.zh: 累轉魯郡太守。

translations.literal: He was transferred in succession to become Administrator of Lu Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He later served in succession as administrator of Lu Commandery.

sentences.zh: 善果母崔，賢明曉政治，嘗坐閤內聽善果處決，或當理則悅，有不可，則引至床下，責愧之。

translations.literal: Shangguo's mother, Lady Cui, was wise and understood governance; she would sit inside the inner chamber listening to Shangguo pass judgment—when a decision was right she was pleased; when not, she would pull him to the bedside and reproach and shame him.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguo's mother, Lady Cui, was intelligent and versed in affairs of state. She would sit in the inner hall and listen as he decided cases: if his ruling was sound she was pleased; if not, she would draw him to her bedside and rebuke him until he felt ashamed.

sentences.zh: 故善果所至有績，號清吏。

translations.literal: Therefore wherever Shangguo went he had achievements, and was called a pure official.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever Shangguo served he left a record of accomplishment, and men called him an incorruptible magistrate.

sentences.zh: 嘗與武威太守樊子蓋考為天下第一，煬帝賜物千段、黃金百兩。

translations.literal: Once he and Fan Zigai, Administrator of Wuwei, were rated first in the empire in performance review; Emperor Yang bestowed a thousand bolts of goods and a hundred taels of gold.
translations.idiomatic: On one occasion he and Fan Zigai, prefect of Wuwei, were ranked the top administrators in the realm; Emperor Yang rewarded them with a thousand bolts of silk and a hundred taels of gold.

sentences.zh: 再遷大理卿。

translations.literal: He was again transferred to become Minister of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed minister of justice.

sentences.zh: 突厥圍帝雁門，以守禦功拜右光祿大夫。

translations.literal: When the Turks besieged the Emperor at Yanmen, for his defense he was appointed Right Grand Master for Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks besieged the emperor at Yanmen, he was made right grand master for splendid happiness for his part in the defense.

sentences.zh: 從幸江都。

translations.literal: He followed the Emperor to Jiangdu.
translations.idiomatic: He accompanied the emperor to Jiangdu.

sentences.zh: 宇文化及弑逆，署民部尚書，從至聊城。

translations.literal: When Yuwen Huaji committed regicide, he was appointed Minister of the Ministry of Revenue and followed him to Liaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: After Yuwen Huaji murdered the emperor, Huaji made him minister of revenue and took him to Liaocheng.

sentences.zh: 淮安王神通攻之，善果督戰，中流矢。

translations.literal: Prince Huai'an Wang Shentong attacked; Shangguo directed the battle and was struck by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince Huai'an, Wang Shentong, laid siege to the city, Shangguo commanded the defense and was hit by a stray arrow.

sentences.zh: 神通解。

translations.literal: Shentong lifted the siege.
translations.idiomatic: Shentong then withdrew.

sentences.zh: 俄為竇建德所獲，王琮讓之曰：「公，隋大臣，自尊夫人亡，名稱衰。

translations.literal: Soon he was captured by Dou Jiande; Wang Cong rebuked him, saying: "Sir, you are a Sui minister; ever since your noble wife died, your reputation has declined.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was taken by Dou Jiande. Wang Cong reproached him: "You were a minister of Sui. Ever since your wife died, your standing has fallen.

sentences.zh: 今以忠臣子為逆賊徇命至傷夷，謂何？」

translations.literal: Now, as the son of a loyal minister, you exhaust yourself in the rebels' service until you are wounded—what do you call this?"
translations.idiomatic: And now the son of a loyal father fights for traitors hard enough to take an arrow—what name do you give that?"

sentences.zh: 善果慚，欲自殺，或止之，得不死。

translations.literal: Shangguo was ashamed, wished to kill himself; someone stopped him, and he did not die.
translations.idiomatic: Shangguo was mortified and tried to take his own life; others restrained him, and he survived.

sentences.zh: 建德不之禮，乃歸神通。

translations.literal: Jiande did not treat him with courtesy, and so he returned to Shentong.
translations.idiomatic: Jiande showed him no honor, and he went back to Shentong.

sentences.zh: 送京師，擢太子左庶子，更封滎陽郡公。

translations.literal: Sent to the capital, he was promoted to Left Assistant to the Heir Apparent and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Xingyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Once escorted to the capital, he was made left assistant to the heir apparent and created duke of Xingyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 數為太子陳得失。

translations.literal: He repeatedly counseled the Heir Apparent on strengths and failings.
translations.idiomatic: He often advised the heir apparent on what the court was doing well and where it went wrong.

sentences.zh: 未幾，檢校大理卿，兼民部尚書。

translations.literal: Before long, he was appointed acting Minister of Justice, with concurrent duty as Minister of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he was made acting minister of justice while also serving as minister of revenue.

sentences.zh: 奉法持正，風績顯公卿間。

translations.literal: Upholding the law and maintaining rectitude, his reputation was conspicuous among the grandees.
translations.idiomatic: He enforced the law without favor and kept an upright course, and his standing among the high ministers was widely noted.

sentences.zh: 詔與裴寂等十人每奏事若侍得升殿，而從父兄元璹亦與，時以為榮。

translations.literal: An edict grouped him with Pei Ji and nine others—whenever they presented memorials, if they were attendants they could ascend the hall—and his paternal cousin Yuan Su was also included; the times considered it an honor.
translations.idiomatic: An edict named him one of ten men, including Pei Ji, who whenever they memorialized the throne might enter the hall if they were in attendance; his older cousin Yuan Su was among them as well, and contemporaries regarded the privilege as a mark of distinction.

sentences.zh: 坐事免。

translations.literal: He was dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was removed from office because of a misconduct charge.

sentences.zh: 會山東平，持節為招撫大使。

translations.literal: When Shandong was pacified, he was granted the credential of commissioner and made Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When the east had been pacified, he received imperial credentials and was appointed pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 以選舉失實除名。

translations.literal: He was struck from the rolls for nominating candidates falsely.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his name from the registers after his recommendations proved false.

sentences.zh: 後歷刑部尚書。

translations.literal: Later he served successively as Minister of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: He later held the post of minister of punishments.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，出為岐州刺史，以累去。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he was sent out as Prefect of Qi Prefecture and left on account of accumulated faults.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhenguan reign he was sent out as prefect of Qi Prefecture but was dismissed after repeated faults.

sentences.zh: 復拜江州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Prefect of Jiang Prefecture and died in office.
translations.idiomatic: He was later reappointed prefect of Jiang Prefecture and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 元璹，字德芳，隋沛國公譯之子。

translations.literal: Yuan Su, courtesy name Defang, was a son of Pei Guo Gong Yi of Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Su, whose courtesy name was Defang, was the son of Duke of Pei State Yi under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 性察慧，愛尚文藝。

translations.literal: By nature perceptive and intelligent, he loved and esteemed literature and arts.
translations.idiomatic: Quick of mind by nature, he delighted in letters and the arts.

sentences.zh: 以父功拜儀同，襲爵。

translations.literal: On account of his father's merit he was appointed Corps Commandant and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: Thanks to his father's service he was made a corps commandant and succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 累遷右衛將軍，更封莘國公。

translations.literal: He was promoted in succession to General of the Right Guard and re-enfeoffed as Duke of Shen State.
translations.idiomatic: He rose in turn to general of the right guard and was re-created duke of Shen State.

sentences.zh: 大業末，出為文城郡守。

translations.literal: At the end of Daye he was sent out as Administrator of Wencheng Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Daye reign he was posted as administrator of Wencheng Commandery.

sentences.zh: 高祖兵興，遣將張綸西略地，攻拔其城，系致軍門，釋之，授太常卿。

translations.literal: When Gaozu raised his army, he sent General Zhang Lun west to seize territory; Lun captured the city, bound him and brought him to the army gate, then released him and appointed him Minister of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: When Gaozu first took up arms, he dispatched General Zhang Lun to expand westward. Lun stormed the city, bound Yuan Su, and brought him before the army, then freed him and made him minister of imperial sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 與襄武王琛使突厥，還為參旗將軍。

translations.literal: Together with Prince Xiangwu Wang Chen he was envoy to the Turks; on return he became General of Canqi Banner.
translations.idiomatic: He went with Prince Xiangwu, Wang Chen, on an embassy to the Turks, and after returning was appointed general of the Canqi banner.

sentences.zh: 元璹習軍旅事，帝令教諸屯軍法。

translations.literal: Yuan Su was versed in military affairs; the Emperor ordered him to teach military regulations to the various garrison troops.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Su knew camp discipline well, and the emperor had him instruct the garrison forces in military law.

sentences.zh: 劉武周將宋金剛與突厥處羅可汗犄角寇汾、晉，元璹諭罷可汗兵，不聽，乃進為武周援。

translations.literal: Liu Wuzhou's general Song Jingang and Turkic Chuluo Khan cooperated in pincer raids on Fen and Jin; Yuan Su urged the khan to withdraw his troops, but the khan would not listen, and so he advanced to aid Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Wuzhou's commander Song Jingang and the Turkic khan Chuluo struck Fen and Jin in concert, Yuan Su persuaded the khan to pull back his men. The khan refused, so Yuan Su marched on to reinforce Wuzhou.

sentences.zh: 會暴疾，其下意元璹置毒，囚之。

translations.literal: He suddenly fell violently ill; his subordinates suspected Yuan Su of poisoning and imprisoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He then fell suddenly and gravely ill; his followers suspected Yuan Su of poisoning him and had him bound.

sentences.zh: 處羅死，頡利立，留帳中數年。

translations.literal: Chuluo died and Jieli succeeded; he was kept in the khan's tent for several years.
translations.idiomatic: When Chuluo died and Jieli took the throne, Yuan Su was detained in the khan's camp for years.

sentences.zh: 帝既許可汗婚，元璹始得還。

translations.literal: Once the Emperor had promised the khan a marriage alliance, Yuan Su was finally able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only after the emperor pledged a marriage alliance with the khan was Yuan Su allowed to come home.

sentences.zh: 帝勞曰：「卿不辱於虜，可輩蘇武、張騫矣。」

translations.literal: The Emperor consoled him, saying: "You did not disgrace yourself among the barbarians—you may be ranked with Su Wu and Zhang Qian."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor welcomed him with praise: "You bore captivity without shame. You stand in the company of Su Wu and Zhang Qian."

sentences.zh: 拜鴻臚卿，母喪免。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of State Hospitality; on his mother's mourning he was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: He was made minister of state hospitality, then left office to mourn his mother.

sentences.zh: 會突厥提精騎數十萬，身自將攻太原，詔即苫次起元璹持節往勞。

translations.literal: When the Turks brought tens of thousands of elite cavalry and personally led an attack on Taiyuan, an edict immediately called Yuan Su from his mourning hut to go with credentials to console them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Turks mustered several hundred thousand picked horsemen and the khan himself marched on Taiyuan, an edict summoned Yuan Su from his mourning shelter and sent him with credentials to offer condolences.

sentences.zh: 既至，虜以不信咎中國，元璹隨語折讓，無所屈，徐乃數其背約，突厥愧服。

translations.literal: When he arrived, the barbarians blamed China for breach of faith; Yuan Su rebutted them as the talk unfolded, yielding in nothing; only then did he slowly enumerate their violations of treaty, and the Turks submitted in shame.
translations.idiomatic: On arrival the Turks accused the court of bad faith. Yuan Su answered point by point without giving ground, then calmly listed their broken promises until they were shamed into submission.

sentences.zh: 因好謂頡利曰：「突厥得唐地無所用，唐得突厥不可臣而使，兩不為用而相攻伐，何哉？

translations.literal: Thereupon he kindly said to Jieli: "Turks gain nothing from Tang territory; Tang cannot make Turks subjects and employ them—why fight when neither side benefits?
translations.idiomatic: Then he spoke gently to Jieli: "What use is Tang land to the Turks? And Tang cannot turn Turks into obedient subjects. If neither side gains, why keep raiding each other?

sentences.zh: 今掠財資，劫人口，皆入所部，可汗一不得，豈若僕旗接好，則金玉重幣一歸可汗。

translations.literal: Now you plunder wealth and seize people, yet all enter your subordinates' hands—the khan gets not one thing; would it not be better to keep friendly relations under my banner, so that gold, jade, and heavy gifts all go to the khan?
translations.idiomatic: Every raid fills your officers' pockets, not yours. Would it not be better to stand as friends beneath my banner, so that gold, jade, and rich tribute flow straight to the khan?

sentences.zh: 且唐有天下，約可汗為兄弟，使驛銜箠於道，今坐受其利不肯，乃蔑德貽怨，自取勞苦，若何？」

translations.literal: Moreover Tang holds the empire and has pledged brotherhood with the khan, with courier stations linking whip to whip along the road—you sit receiving profit yet refuse it, thus scorning virtue and inviting resentment, bringing hardship on yourself; how can this be?"
translations.idiomatic: Tang rules the realm and treats your khan as a brother, with post stations lining the roads. You refuse profit already offered, slight our good faith, and invite ill will—only to wear yourselves out. How does that serve you?"

sentences.zh: 頡利當其言，引還。

translations.literal: Jieli accepted his words and withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Jieli took his counsel to heart and led his men back.

sentences.zh: 太宗賜書曰：「知公口伐，可汗如約，遂使邊火息燧，朕何惜金石賜於公哉！」

translations.literal: Taizong wrote: "Knowing your verbal warfare, the khan kept the agreement—thus border beacon fires were extinguished; why would I begrudge gold and stone bestowed upon you!"
translations.idiomatic: Taizong wrote in reply: "Your tongue did what armies could not—the khan kept peace, and the frontier beacons went dark. Why should I stint gold and jade in rewarding you?"

sentences.zh: 貞觀三年，復使突厥，還言：「夷狄以馬羊准盛衰，今突厥六畜不蕃，人色若菜，牙內飯粟化為血，不三年必亡。」

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhenguan he was again envoy to the Turks; on return he said: "Barbarians take horses and sheep as measure of rise and decline; now the Turks' six livestock do not multiply, people's complexions are like vegetables, and rice in the camp turns to blood—in less than three years they will perish."
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Zhenguan he went again to the Turks. On returning he reported: "The nomads reckon strength by horses and sheep. Their herds no longer breed, their faces look like wilted greens, and grain in the camps turns to blood in the pot—they cannot last three years."

sentences.zh: 無幾，突厥果敗。

translations.literal: Before long the Turks were indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Turks collapsed, just as he had said.

sentences.zh: 後轉左武侯大將軍，坐事免。

translations.literal: Later he was transferred to Grand General of the Left Militant Guard and dismissed on account of an offense.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made grand general of the left militant guard but was removed after an offense.

sentences.zh: 起為宜州刺史，以老致仕。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Prefect of Yizhou and retired on account of age.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to serve as prefect of Yizhou and later retired because of old age.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈幽州刺史，諡曰簡。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Prefect of You Prefecture, posthumous name Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When he died he was posthumously made prefect of You Prefecture, with the posthumous name Jian.

sentences.zh: 元璹幹敏，所至常有譽。

translations.literal: Yuan Su was capable and quick-witted; wherever he went he usually won praise.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Su was forceful and sharp; nearly everywhere he served he earned a good name.

sentences.zh: 五聘絕域，危不脫，終不自為解。

translations.literal: Five missions to distant lands, in danger he did not escape; to the end he never excused himself.
translations.idiomatic: Sent five times to far barbarian courts, he never fled when peril closed in and never tried to explain away his duty.

sentences.zh: 然譯事後母不謹，隋文帝嘗賜《孝經》愧勖之；

translations.literal: Yet Yi was not strict with his stepmother, and Emperor Wen of Sui once bestowed the Classic of Filial Piety to shame and encourage him;
translations.idiomatic: Yet his father Yi had failed in duty toward his stepmother, and Emperor Wen of Sui once sent him the Classic of Filial Piety to rebuke and exhort him;

sentences.zh: 至元璹亦不以孝聞，士醜其行。

translations.literal: down to Yuan Su, who also was not famed for filial piety—the gentry found their conduct shameful.
translations.idiomatic: and Yuan Su too won no reputation for filial conduct, so men of breeding looked on the family with distaste.

sentences.zh: 從孫杲，知名武后世，終天官侍郎。

translations.literal: His collateral descendant Gao was famed in the Wu Zong reign era and ended as Vice Minister of the Celestial Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: A collateral descendant, Gao, became well known in the Wu Zong reign and ended his career as vice minister of the celestial bureau.

sentences.zh: 權萬紀權萬紀，其先出天水，後徙京兆，為萬年人。

translations.literal: Quan Wanji—Quan Wanji: his ancestors came from Tianshui, later moved to Jingzhao, and were people of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Quan Wanji came from a line originally of Tianshui that later settled in Jingzhao and became natives of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 父琢玠，隋匡州刺史，以愨願聞。

translations.literal: His father Zhuojie was Prefect of Kuangzhou in Sui, known for integrity and good will.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhuojie had been prefect of Kuangzhou under the Sui and was known for steadfast honesty.

sentences.zh: 萬紀悻直廉約，自潮州刺史擢治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Wanji was obstinate, upright, and frugal; from Prefect of Chaozhou he was promoted to Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji was blunt, upright, and austere; he rose from prefect of Chaozhou to imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 尚書右僕射房玄齡、侍中王珪掌內外官考，萬紀劾其不平，太宗按狀，珪不伏。

translations.literal: Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Fang Xuanling and Attendant-in-Ordinary Wang Gui managed inner and outer official evaluations; Wanji impeached them for unfairness; Taizong investigated the case and Gui would not submit.
translations.idiomatic: When the right vice director Fang Xuanling and the attendant Wang Gui oversaw evaluations of inner and outer officials, Wanji charged them with bias. Taizong reviewed the case, but Wang Gui refused to concede.

sentences.zh: 魏征奏言：「房玄齡等皆大臣，所考有私，萬紀在考堂無訂正，今而彈發，非誠心為國者。」

translations.literal: Wei Zheng memorialized: "Fang Xuanling and the others are all great ministers; in their evaluations there was partiality, yet Wanji in the evaluation hall made no corrections—now he impeaches them; this is not sincerely serving the state.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng argued: "Men like Fang Xuanling are chief ministers. If their grading was unfair, Wanji should have corrected it in the review hall. To impeach them only afterward is not honest service to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝乃置之，然以為不阿貴近，繇是獎禮。

translations.literal: The Emperor thereupon dropped the matter, yet considered him not to favor the noble and close, and hence rewarded and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor let the charge drop, yet admired Wanji for not truckling to the powerful and therefore singled him out for reward.

sentences.zh: 萬紀又建言：「宇文智及受隋恩，賊殺其君，萬世共棄，今其子乃任千牛，請斥屏以懲不軌。」

translations.literal: Wanji also submitted a proposal: "Yuwen Zhiji received Sui grace yet murdered his lord—the age universally casts him aside—yet now his son holds the post of Thousand-Ox; I request he be expelled to punish lawlessness.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji also urged: "Yuwen Zhiji owed the Sui dynasty everything, then killed his sovereign—a crime all the world condemns—yet his son now serves as a thousand-ox attendant. Expel him as a warning to the lawless.

sentences.zh: 帝從之。

translations.literal: The Emperor agreed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted the proposal.

sentences.zh: 萬紀與侍御史李仁發既以言得進，頗掉罄自肆，眾情懍懍。

translations.literal: Wanji and Censor Li Renfa, having gained advancement through their words, became quite overbearing and unrestrained; public sentiment was fearful.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji and the censor Li Renfa, elevated because of their outspokenness, grew arrogant and overbearing, and the court grew uneasy.

sentences.zh: 征奏：「萬紀等暗大體，詆訐彈射皆不實，陛下收其一切，遂敢附下罔上，釣強直名，迷奪聖明，以小謀大，群下離心。

translations.literal: Wei Zheng memorialized: "Wanji and the others ignore the larger principles; their slanders and impeachments are all unfounded; Your Majesty accepts everything from them, and so they dare to attach to subordinates and deceive superiors, fishing for a reputation for blunt rectitude, obscuring Your Majesty's clarity, using small schemes against great ones—the subordinates lose heart.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Zheng wrote: "Wanji and his like ignore the larger good. Their accusations are hollow, yet Your Majesty indulges every charge, so they court the lower ranks and mislead their betters, angling for a name as blunt truth-tellers while clouding your judgment. They use petty tricks against great ministers, and the whole court loses faith.

sentences.zh: 如玄齡等且不得申，況疏賤之臣哉？」

translations.literal: If men like Xuanling cannot even defend themselves, how much less low and humble officials?
translations.idiomatic: If even Fang Xuanling cannot answer them, what chance has any obscure clerk?

sentences.zh: 帝寤，徙萬紀散騎常侍，而免仁發。

translations.literal: The Emperor came to his senses, transferred Wanji to Palace Attendant and dismissed Renfa.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor took the point, moved Wanji to palace attendant, and removed Li Renfa from office.

sentences.zh: 數年，復召萬紀為持書御史，即奏言：「宣、饒部中可鑿山冶銀，歲取數百萬。」

translations.literal: Several years later Wanji was again summoned as Credential-bearing Censor; he immediately memorialized: "In Xuan and Rao prefectures ore can be mined to smelt silver, yielding several million per year.
translations.idiomatic: Years later Wanji was recalled as credential-bearing censor and at once proposed: "In the Xuan and Rao regions mountains can be opened to refine silver, bringing in several million a year.

sentences.zh: 帝讓曰：「天子所乏，嘉謀善政有益於下者。

translations.literal: The Emperor rebuked him: "What the Son of Heaven lacks is good counsel and sound policy that benefit the people.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor snapped back: "What an emperor needs is wise counsel and policies that help the people.

sentences.zh: 公不推賢進善，乃以利規我，欲方我漢桓、靈邪？」

translations.literal: You do not recommend the worthy and advance the good, yet use profit to gauge me—do you wish to compare me to Emperors Huan and Ling of Han?
translations.idiomatic: You do not bring forward the worthy; you try to measure me by profit. Do you mean to rank me with the Huan and Ling emperors of Han?

sentences.zh: 斥使還第。

translations.literal: He was dismissed and sent home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent him home in disgrace.

sentences.zh: 久之，由御史中丞進尚書左丞，出為西韓州刺史。

translations.literal: After a long time, from Vice Censor-in-Chief he was promoted to Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs and sent out as Prefect of Xihan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Long afterward he rose from vice censor-in-chief to left vice director of the department of state affairs, then went out as prefect of Xihan.

sentences.zh: 徙吳王長史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Senior Tutor of the Prince of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as senior tutor to the prince of Wu.

sentences.zh: 王畏其直，善遇之。

translations.literal: The Prince feared his bluntness and treated him well.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, wary of his bluntness, treated him with special respect.

sentences.zh: 齊王祐不奉法，帝素奇萬紀能左右吳王者，乃徙為祐長史。

translations.literal: Prince of Qi You did not obey the law; the Emperor had long considered Wanji able to influence the Prince of Wu, and so transferred him to be You's Senior Tutor.
translations.idiomatic: The prince of Qi, You, scorned the law. The emperor had long thought Wanji could steady the prince of Wu, so he moved him to serve as You's senior tutor.

sentences.zh: 祐暱比群小，萬紀驟諫不入，即條過失以聞。

translations.literal: You was intimate with base companions; Wanji repeatedly remonstrated but was not heeded, and so listed his faults and reported them upstream.
translations.idiomatic: You kept company with worthless men. Wanji remonstrated again and again without effect, then catalogued his faults and reported them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 帝遣劉德威按問，因召祐入朝。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent Liu Dewei to investigate, and summoned You to court.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dispatched Liu Dewei to inquire into the matter and ordered You to the capital.

sentences.zh: 祐恐，與所嬖燕弘亮謀殺之，而萬紀先引道。

translations.literal: You was afraid and with his favorite Yan Hongliang plotted to kill him, but Wanji had already set out on the road.
translations.idiomatic: You, in fear, conspired with his favorite Yan Hongliang to murder Wanji, but Wanji had already taken to the road.

sentences.zh: 祐遣弘亮馳彀騎追擊，斬首，殊支體，投圊中。

translations.literal: You sent Hongliang with swift cavalry in pursuit; they beheaded him, dismembered the corpse, and cast it into a privy.
translations.idiomatic: You sent Hongliang with fast cavalry in pursuit. They cut off Wanji's head, hacked apart his body, and threw the pieces into a cesspit.

sentences.zh: 又殺典軍韋文振。

translations.literal: He also killed Army Supervisor Wei Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: They also killed the army supervisor Wei Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 文振本以校尉從帝征伐，以質謹自將，帝使事祐，典廄馬，切諫不納，輒見萬紀道之，故祐內嘗忿疾。

translations.literal: Wenzhen had originally followed the Emperor on campaign as a company commander; through integrity and prudence he conducted himself; the Emperor had him serve You, overseeing the stable horses; he remonstrated sharply but was not accepted, and would often tell Wanji; hence You inwardly often resented him.
translations.idiomatic: Wenzhen had campaigned with the emperor as a company commander, distinguished for strict and careful conduct. The emperor assigned him to You to manage the stables. He counseled bluntly and was ignored, and often confided in Wanji, so You had long nursed a private hatred of him.

sentences.zh: 萬紀死，文振懼，馳去，追騎獲之。

translations.literal: When Wanji died, Wenzhen was afraid and fled on horseback; pursuing riders caught him.
translations.idiomatic: After Wanji was killed, Wenzhen fled in terror; mounted pursuers overtook and seized him.

sentences.zh: 祐平，贈萬紀齊州都督、武都郡公，食二千戶，諡曰敢，文振左武衛將軍、襄陽縣公，食千戶。

translations.literal: When You was pacified, Wanji was posthumously appointed Military Governor of Qi Prefecture and Duke of Wudu Commandery with an estate of two thousand households, posthumous name Gan; Wenzhen was posthumously appointed General of the Left Martial Guard and Duke of Xiangyang County with an estate of one thousand households.
translations.idiomatic: Once You's rebellion was crushed, Wanji was posthumously made military governor of Qi Prefecture and duke of Wudu Commandery with an estate of two thousand households, posthumous name Gan; Wenzhen was posthumously made general of the left martial guard and duke of Xiangyang County with an estate of one thousand households.

sentences.zh: 萬紀子玄初，高宗時兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Wanji's son Xuanchu, in the Gaozong reign served as Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Wanji's son Xuanchu served as vice minister of war early in the Gaozong reign.

sentences.zh: 族孫 懷恩懷恩，萬紀族孫。

translations.literal: Collateral descendant Huai'en—Huai'en was Wanji's collateral descendant.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was a collateral descendant of Wanji.

sentences.zh: 祖弘壽，為隋臨汾司倉書佐，高祖平京師，擢太僕卿、盧國公，卒，諡曰恭。

translations.literal: His grandfather Hongshou was a clerical assistant in the granary office of Linfen in Sui; when Gaozu pacified the capital he was promoted to Minister of the Imperial Stud and Duke of Lu State; he died, posthumous name Gong.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Hongshou had been a granary clerk at Linfen under the Sui. When Gaozu took the capital, Hongshou was raised to minister of the imperial stud and created duke of Lu State; at his death he received the posthumous name Gong.

sentences.zh: 故懷恩以廕累遷尚乘奉禦，襲爵。

translations.literal: Hence Huai'en by yin privilege rose in succession to Master of the Imperial Mount and inherited the title.
translations.idiomatic: By inherited privilege Huai'en rose in turn to master of the imperial mount and succeeded to the title.

sentences.zh: 馭人安畢羅為高宗所寵，見帝，戲慢不恭，懷恩奏事，適見之，退杖四十。

translations.literal: His groom An Biluo was favored by Gaozong; seeing the Emperor he was playful and disrespectful; Huai'en was presenting a memorial and happened to see it; on leaving he was caned forty strokes.
translations.idiomatic: His groom An Biluo enjoyed Gaozong's favor and once behaved insolently before the emperor. Huai'en, arriving to present a memorial, witnessed it; when he withdrew he had Biluo beaten forty strokes with the staff.

sentences.zh: 帝嗟賞曰：「良吏也！」

translations.literal: The Emperor sighed in admiration: "A good official!"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor exclaimed with approval: "There is a magistrate after my own heart!"

sentences.zh: 擢萬年令。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Magistrate of Wannian.
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was promoted to magistrate of Wannian.

sentences.zh: 賞罰明，見惡輒取。

translations.literal: Rewards and punishments were clear; when he saw wrongdoing he immediately acted.
translations.idiomatic: He ruled with clear reward and punishment, striking at wrong the moment he saw it.

sentences.zh: 時語曰：「寧飲三鬥塵，無逢權懷恩。」

translations.literal: At the time people said: "Better to drink three pecks of dust than encounter Quan Huai'en."
translations.idiomatic: A saying of the day ran: "I'd rather swallow three pecks of dust than run into Quan Huai'en.

sentences.zh: 其姿狀沈毅，每盛服，妻子不敢仰視。

translations.literal: His bearing was solemn and resolute; whenever he wore full ceremonial dress, his wife and children did not dare look up at him.
translations.idiomatic: He was imposing and grave of mien; dressed in full regalia, even his wife and children did not dare meet his gaze."

sentences.zh: 更慶、萊、衛、邢、宋五州刺史，洛州長史。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Prefect of the five prefectures of Gengqing, Lai, Wei, Xing, and Song, and as Chief Secretary of Luo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He held office in turn as prefect of Gengqing, Lai, Wei, Xing, and Song, and as chief secretary of Luo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 所居威名赫然，吏重足立。

translations.literal: Wherever he served his aweful reputation was conspicuous; clerks stood with feet placed together.
translations.idiomatic: Wherever he held office his stern fame was unmistakable, and subordinates stood as if afraid to move.

sentences.zh: 嘗過汴州，時刺史楊德幹亦以嚴稱，與懷恩名相埒。

translations.literal: Once he passed through Bian Prefecture; at the time the prefect Yang Degan was also famed for severity, and his reputation matched Huai'en's.
translations.idiomatic: Once when passing through Bian Prefecture he found the prefect Yang Degan, himself notorious for harsh rule, a rival in reputation.

sentences.zh: 汴橋新成，立木中途，止過車者。

translations.literal: The Bian Bridge had just been completed; a pole was set up mid-span to halt passing carts.
translations.idiomatic: A newly finished bridge at Bian had a post erected in the middle to stop traffic from crossing.

sentences.zh: 懷恩適過之，示德幹曰：「民不可止邪，焉用此？」

translations.literal: Huai'en happened to pass by and, indicating it to Degan, said: "Cannot the people be restrained? What need is there for this?"
translations.idiomatic: Huai'en was just passing and, pointing it out to Degan, said: "If you cannot govern the people without such devices, what good are you? Why resort to this?

sentences.zh: 德幹慚服。

translations.literal: Degan was ashamed and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Degan, abashed, conceded the point."

sentences.zh: 遷益州大都督府長史，卒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Chief Secretary of the Great Capital Protectorate of Yizhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: He was made chief secretary of the Yizhou metropolitan protectorate and died in that post.

sentences.zh: 從子楚璧，為左領軍衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: His nephew Chu Bi served as Army Adjutant of the Left Leading Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: His nephew Chu Bi held the post of army adjutant in the Left Leading Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在東都，楚璧乃與李迥秀子齊損、陳倉尉盧玢、左屯營長上折沖周履濟等謀反，以兄子梁山詐為襄王子，號光帝，擁營兵百餘夜入官城，欲劫留守王志愔，不克。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was at the Eastern Capital, Chu Bi together with Li Hui Xiu's son Qi Sun, Chencang Commandant Lu Bin, Left Tunwei Camp Senior Soldier and Colonel of the Sixth Rank Zhou Lüji, and others plotted rebellion; with his elder brother's son Liangshan he falsely claimed to be a son of the Prince of Xiang, styled himself Emperor Guang, and with more than a hundred garrison troops entered the palace city by night intending to seize the custodian Wang Zhihui, but failed.
translations.idiomatic: While Xuanzong was at Luoyang, Chu Bi joined Qi Sun, son of Li Hui Xiu, Chencang commandant Lu Bin, Left Tunwei camp officer Zhou Lüji, and others in a plot. They put forward his nephew Liangshan as a false heir of the Prince of Xiang, styled him Emperor Guang, and led more than a hundred garrison soldiers into the palace at night to seize the custodian Wang Zhihui, but the attempt failed.

sentences.zh: 遲明，兵斬楚璧等，傳首東都，籍其家。

translations.literal: At dawn soldiers beheaded Chu Bi and the others, sent their heads to the Eastern Capital, and confiscated their families' property.
translations.idiomatic: By dawn the troops had beheaded Chu Bi and his accomplices, sent their heads to Luoyang, and seized their families' estates.

sentences.zh: 閻立德閻讓，字立德，以字行，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Yan Lide—Yan Rang, courtesy name Lide, known by his courtesy name, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Lide, whose original name was Yan Rang and courtesy name Lide, was known by his courtesy name and came from Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 父毘，為隋殿內少監，本以工藝進，故立德與弟立本皆機巧有思。

translations.literal: His father Pi was Sui Palace Attendant Within; originally entered office through craftsmanship, so Lide and his younger brother Liben were both ingenious and thoughtful.
translations.idiomatic: His father Pi had been a palace attendant within under the Sui and had risen through the crafts; Lide and his younger brother Liben inherited both skill and inventive minds.

sentences.zh: 武德初，為秦王府士曹參軍，從平東都。

translations.literal: Early in Wude he served as Staff Officer of the Princely Household in the Prince of Qin's mansion and followed in pacifying the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Wude reign he was a staff officer in the Prince of Qin's household and took part in the pacification of Luoyang.

sentences.zh: 遷尚衣奉禦，制袞冕六服、腰輿、傘扇，咸有典法。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Director of Imperial Tailoring and designed the six sacrificial robes, sedan chairs, umbrellas, and fans—all according to canonical norms.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to director of imperial tailoring, he devised the six ceremonial robes, sedan chairs, umbrellas, and fans, each to proper canonical standard.

sentences.zh: 貞觀初，歷將作少匠、大安縣男。

translations.literal: Early in Zhenguan he served in succession as Assistant Master of Palace Construction and Baron of Da'an County.
translations.idiomatic: At the opening of the Zhenguan reign he rose in turn to assistant master of palace construction and was created baron of Da'an County.

sentences.zh: 護治獻陵，拜大匠。

translations.literal: He oversaw repair of Xian Mausoleum and was appointed Grand Master of Construction.
translations.idiomatic: Put in charge of work on Xian Mausoleum, he was appointed grand master of construction.

sentences.zh: 文德皇后崩，攝司空，營昭陵，坐弛職免。

translations.literal: When Empress Wende died he served as acting Minister of Works and built Zhaoling; he was dismissed for dereliction of duty.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wende's death he acted as minister of works and oversaw Zhaoling, but was removed for neglect of duty.

sentences.zh: 起為博州刺史。

translations.literal: He was recalled as Prefect of Bo Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was later restored and sent out as prefect of Bo Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太宗幸洛陽，詔立德按爽塏建離宮清暑，乃度地汝州西山，控汝水，睨廣成澤，號襄城宮，役凡百餘萬。

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong visited Luoyang, an edict had Lide select high, dry ground to build a summer retreat palace; he measured land at the Western Hills of Ru Prefecture, overlooking the Ru River and facing Guangcheng Marsh; it was named Xiangcheng Palace, and the laborers totaled more than a million.
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong went to Luoyang, Lide was ordered to find high, dry ground for a summer palace. He chose the western hills of Ru Prefecture, above the Ru River and overlooking Guangcheng Marsh, and built Xiangcheng Palace at a cost of more than a million laborers.

sentences.zh: 宮成，煩燠不可居，帝廢之，以賜百姓，坐免官。

translations.literal: When the palace was finished it was stifling and unbearable to live in; the Emperor abandoned it and gave it to the common people, and Lide was dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Once finished the palace proved hot and uninhabitable. The emperor abandoned it and gave it to the people, and Lide lost his post.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復為大匠，即洪州造浮海大航五百艘，遂從征遼，攝殿中監，規築土山，破安市城。

translations.literal: Before long he was again Grand Master of Construction; at Hongzhou he built five hundred great ocean-going ships, then followed the campaign against Liaodong as acting Palace Attendant Within, planning and building earthen mounds to breach Anshi city.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again grand master of construction. At Hongzhou he built five hundred large seagoing vessels, then joined the Liaodong campaign as acting palace attendant within, directing the earthen siege mounds that broke Anshi.

sentences.zh: 師還，至遼澤，亙二百里，淖不可通，立德築道為橋樑，無留行。

translations.literal: When the army returned and reached Liaose Marsh, stretching two hundred li, the mud was impassable; Lide built a road and bridges, and no one was delayed.
translations.idiomatic: On the march home the army struck Liaose Marsh, two hundred li of mire. Lide built a road and bridges across it so the column never stalled.

sentences.zh: 帝悅，賜予良厚。

translations.literal: The Emperor was pleased and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and heaped rewards upon him.

sentences.zh: 又營翠微、玉華二宮，擢工部尚書。

translations.literal: He also built the Cuiwei and Yuhua palaces and was promoted to Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: He later constructed the Cuiwei and Yuhua palaces and was raised to minister of works.

sentences.zh: 帝崩，復攝司空，典陵事，以勞進爵大安縣公。

translations.literal: When the Emperor died he again served as acting Minister of Works and managed mausoleum affairs; for his labor he was promoted to Duke of Da'an County.
translations.idiomatic: After Taizong's death he again acted as minister of works and oversaw the imperial tomb, and for that service was created duke of Da'an County.

sentences.zh: 永征五年，高宗幸萬年宮，留守京師，領徒四萬治京城。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Yonghui, when Emperor Gaozong visited Wannian Palace, Lide remained in the capital as custodian and led forty thousand laborers to repair the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Yonghui, while Gaozong was at Wannian Palace, Lide stayed behind in the capital and put forty thousand workers to repairing the city.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈吏部尚書、并州都督，陪葬昭陵，諡曰康。

translations.literal: He died; posthumously appointed Minister of Personnel and Military Governor of Bing Prefecture; buried with Zhaoling; posthumous name Kang.
translations.idiomatic: At his death he was posthumously made minister of personnel and military governor of Bing Prefecture, buried at Zhaoling, with the posthumous name Kang.

sentences.zh: 附 閻立本立本，顯慶中以將作大匠代立德為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Appendix: Yan Liben—Liben, in Xianqing as Master of Palace Construction replaced Lide as Minister of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Liben: in the Xianqing era he succeeded Lide as minister of works while serving as master of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 總章元年，以司平太常伯拜右相、博陵縣男。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zongzhang, as Minister of Ritual with the concurrent title of Ping he was appointed Right Chancellor and Baron of Boling County.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zongzhang, already minister of ritual with the concurrent title of ping, he was made right chancellor and created baron of Boling County.

sentences.zh: 初，太宗與侍臣泛舟春苑池，見異鳥容與波上，悅之，詔坐者賦詩，而召立本侔狀。

translations.literal: Initially Emperor Taizong and his attending ministers boated on the Spring Garden pool; seeing a strange bird floating on the water, he was pleased and ordered those seated to compose poems, and summoned Liben to paint its likeness.
translations.idiomatic: Once Taizong went boating on the Spring Garden pool with his ministers. Delighted by a strange bird drifting on the water, he ordered poems from the company and called Liben to sketch the bird.

sentences.zh: 閤外傳呼畫師閻立本，是時已為主爵郎中，俯伏池左，研吮丹粉，望坐者羞悵流汗。

translations.literal: Outside the gate came the call to summon the painter Yan Liben; he was then already Director of Principal Titles; prostrating himself at the left of the pool, he ground and licked cinnabar powder, and gazing at those seated he was ashamed and anxious, sweating.
translations.idiomatic: From outside the gate came the shout for the painter Yan Liben. Already a director of principal titles, he crawled to the pool's edge, ground vermilion, and as he looked up at the courtiers he flushed with shame and sweat.

sentences.zh: 歸戒其子曰：「吾少讀書，文辭不減儕輩，今獨以畫見名，與廝役等，若曹慎毋習！」

translations.literal: Returning he admonished his sons, saying: "From youth I read books; my literary skill does not fall short of my peers; now I alone am known for painting, equal to menial laborers—you be careful not to learn this!"
translations.idiomatic: Back home he warned his sons: "I studied from boyhood and write as well as my peers, yet I am known only for painting and treated like a servant. See that you never take it up!

sentences.zh: 然性所好，雖被訾屈，亦不能罷也。

translations.literal: Yet what his nature favored, though he was scorned and humiliated, he still could not stop.
translations.idiomatic: Yet painting was his nature's delight, and though the work humiliated him, he could not give it up."

sentences.zh: 既輔政，但以應務俗材，無宰相器。

translations.literal: Having assisted in government, he was only competent for routine tasks—not material for a chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Once in high office he proved useful only for routine business and lacked the stature of a true chief minister.

sentences.zh: 時姜恪以戰功擢左相，故時人有「左相宣威沙漠，右相馳譽丹青」之嘲。

translations.literal: At the time Jiang Ke was promoted Left Chancellor for military achievement, so people had the mockery: "The left chancellor spreads might in the desert; the right chancellor spreads fame in painting."
translations.idiomatic: Because Jiang Ke had risen to left chancellor on military merit, wits mocked: "The left chancellor wins glory in the desert; the right chancellor wins glory with his brush."

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，官復舊名，改中書令。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng offices were restored to their old names, and he was changed to Chancellor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Xianheng the old titles were restored and he became chancellor of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 卒，諡曰文貞。

translations.literal: He died; posthumous name Wenzhen.
translations.idiomatic: He died and received the posthumous name Wenzhen.

sentences.zh: 立德孫知微，曾孫用之。

translations.literal: Lide's grandson was Zhiwei; his great-grandson was Yongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Lide's grandson was Zhiwei and his great-grandson Yongzhi.

sentences.zh: 孫 知微知微，聖曆初為豹韜衛將軍。

translations.literal: Grandson Zhiwei—Zhiwei, at the opening of Shenli served as General of the Leopard Battle Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei, Lide's grandson, became general of the leopard battle guard at the start of the Shenli era.

sentences.zh: 武后時，突厥默啜請和親，后遣知微攝春官尚書，持金帛護送武延秀聘其女。

translations.literal: During Empress Wu's time the Turkic khan Moqi requested a marriage alliance; the Empress dispatched Zhiwei as acting Minister of the Spring Office, bearing gold and silk to escort Wu Yanxiu in betrothing Moqi's daughter.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu the Turkic khan Moqi sought a marriage alliance. She sent Zhiwei, acting minister of the spring office, with gold and silk to escort Wu Yanxiu as betrothal envoy for Moqi's daughter.

sentences.zh: 默啜怒非天子子，囚延秀，挾知微入寇趙、定，尊之如可汗，以示華人，自河以北蕭然。

translations.literal: Moqi, angry that the envoy was not the Son of Heaven's son, imprisoned Yanxiu, took Zhiwei on a raid into Zhao and Ding, honored him like a khan to display to the Chinese, and from north of the Yellow River all was desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Moqi, furious that the court had not sent an imperial prince, seized Yanxiu, dragged Zhiwei on raids through Zhao and Ding, and paraded him before Chinese captives as though he were a khan, until the country north of the Yellow River lay waste.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以知微賣國，夷其族。

translations.literal: The court considered Zhiwei a traitor to the state and exterminated his clan.
translations.idiomatic: The court condemned Zhiwei as a traitor and wiped out his entire clan.

sentences.zh: 知微不知，逃還。

translations.literal: Zhiwei did not know this and fled back.
translations.idiomatic: Zhiwei, unaware of the sentence, escaped and returned home.

sentences.zh: 武后業已然，乃曰：「惡臣疾子，賜百官甘心焉。」

translations.literal: Empress Wu, the matter already settled, then said: "Wicked minister, hateful son—let the hundred officials relish their hearts on him."
translations.idiomatic: With the verdict already fixed, Empress Wu declared: "This villain and his vile son—let every official feast his heart on them.

sentences.zh: 於是骨斷臠分，非要職者不能得。

translations.literal: Then bones were broken and flesh carved apart—those without important posts could not obtain any.
translations.idiomatic: His body was hacked to pieces, and only men of rank could claim a portion."

sentences.zh: 子則先，以武三思婿免死。

translations.literal: His son Ze Xian, as son-in-law of Wu Sansi, escaped death.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze Xian survived because he was married into Wu Sansi's house.

sentences.zh: 玄宗在籓時，以善割蒙寵。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong was a prince he was favored for skill at carving.
translations.idiomatic: While still a prince, Xuanzong favored him for his skill at carving.

sentences.zh: 開元中，有司奏擬供奉，姚元崇以為則先刑戮家，又逆人姻屬，不可留京師。

translations.literal: In Kaiyuan the departments proposed him for palace service; Yao Yuanchong thought that Ze Xian's family had suffered execution and that he was kin of a rebel—not to remain in the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the Kaiyuan era the ministries nominated him for palace service, but Yao Yuanchong argued that a man whose family had been executed and who was related to a traitor had no place in the capital.

sentences.zh: 詔曰：「朕在外日，嘗驅使，宜令供奉。」

translations.literal: An edict said: "When I was outside, I used to drive him about; he should be allowed palace service."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor replied: "When I was still a prince I often had him attend me. Let him serve at court."

sentences.zh: 曾孫 用之用之，初為彭州參軍，嘗攝錄事，一日糾愆謬不法數十事，太守以為材。

translations.literal: Great-grandson Yongzhi—Yongzhi, initially Military Adjutant of Peng Prefecture; once acting recording clerk; in one day he corrected dozens of errors of law; the prefect considered him talented.
translations.idiomatic: Yongzhi, Lide's great-grandson, began as military adjutant of Peng Prefecture. Acting as recording clerk for a day, he caught dozens of legal irregularities, and the prefect marked him as able.

sentences.zh: 後舉通事舍人，累遷右衛郎將，知引駕仗。

translations.literal: Later he was recommended as Court Liaison Officer; he rose in succession to Right Guard Commandant and managed the imperial carriage escort.
translations.idiomatic: He was later made a court liaison officer, rose to right guard commandant, and took charge of the imperial carriage escort.

sentences.zh: 金吾將軍李質升殿不解刀，呵卻之，請按以法，左右震悚。

translations.literal: Metal-Fetter General Li Zhi ascended the hall without removing his sword; Yongzhi shouted him back and requested investigation by law; those nearby were shaken in fear.
translations.idiomatic: When Metal-Fetter General Li Zhi entered the hall without sheathing his sword, Yongzhi barked him back and demanded legal punishment; the courtiers trembled.

sentences.zh: 始，有司以三衛執扇登殿，用之奏三衛皆趫悍，不宜升陛邇禦坐，請以宦者代，遂為故事。

translations.literal: Initially the departments had the Three Guards hold fans while ascending the hall; Yongzhi memorialized that the Three Guards were all fierce and bold and not fit to ascend the steps near the imperial seat, and requested eunuchs replace them; this became precedent.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Three Guards had carried the imperial fans up the hall. Yongzhi argued that these men were too rough to stand close to the throne and asked that eunuchs take their place—a practice that then became fixed.

sentences.zh: 天寶中，女為義王玼妃。

translations.literal: In the Tianbao era his daughter became consort of the Prince of Righteousness Ci.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianbao reign his daughter married Prince Ci of Righteousness.

sentences.zh: 終左金吾將軍。

translations.literal: He ended as Left Metal-Fetter General.
translations.idiomatic: He finished his career as left metal-fetter general.

sentences.zh: 蔣儼蔣儼，常州義興人。

translations.literal: Jiang Yan—Jiang Yan, a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Yan was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 擢明經第，為左屯衛兵曹參軍。

translations.literal: Advanced in the Mingjing examination, he served as Army Adjutant of the Left Tunwei Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Passing the Mingjing examination, he became army adjutant of the Left Tunwei Guard.

sentences.zh: 太宗將伐高麗，募為使者，人皆憚行，儼奮曰：「以天子雄武，四夷畏威，蕞爾國敢圖王人？

translations.literal: When Emperor Taizong was about to attack Goguryeo and recruited envoys, all feared the journey; Yan exclaimed: "With the Son of Heaven's martial might, the four barbarians fear his awefulness—a petty state dare plot against the king's envoy?
translations.idiomatic: When Taizong prepared to strike Goguryeo and sought envoys, everyone shrank from the mission. Yan cried out: "With the Son of Heaven's might the four quarters tremble—would this petty kingdom dare lay hands on the emperor's messenger?

sentences.zh: 有如不幸，固吾死所也。」

translations.literal: If by misfortune [I should die], that is precisely where I should die."
translations.idiomatic: If I meet misfortune, that is simply where I am meant to die.

sentences.zh: 遂請行。

translations.literal: Then he requested to go.
translations.idiomatic: With that he volunteered for the mission."

sentences.zh: 為莫離支所囚，以兵脅之，不屈，內窟室中。

translations.literal: He was imprisoned by Mo Liche; threatened with weapons, he did not submit and was confined in an inner pit chamber.
translations.idiomatic: Mo Liche seized and imprisoned him, threatened him with arms, and when he would not yield shut him in an underground cell.

sentences.zh: 高麗平，乃得歸。

translations.literal: When Goguryeo was pacified he was able to return.
translations.idiomatic: Only after Goguryeo fell was he able to come home.

sentences.zh: 帝奇其節，授朝散大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor marveled at his integrity and appointed him Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his steadfastness and made him a gentleman for dispersing affairs.

sentences.zh: 為幽州司馬，劉祥道以巡察使到部，表最狀，擢會州刺史。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Prefect of You Prefecture; when Liu Xiangdao arrived as inspection commissioner he submitted the highest rating and Yan was promoted to Prefect of Hui Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: As vice prefect of You Prefecture he won the top evaluation when Liu Xiangdao came as inspector and was promoted to prefect of Hui.

sentences.zh: 再遷殿中少監，數陳時政病利，高宗輒優納。

translations.literal: He was again promoted to Vice Director of Palace Affairs; repeatedly presenting the ills and benefits of current affairs, Emperor Gaozong always graciously accepted.
translations.idiomatic: Raised to vice director of palace affairs, he often memorialized on the empire's faults and strengths, and Gaozong always heard him with favor.

sentences.zh: 進蒲州刺史，戶產充夥，訴犴積年不平，前刺史踵以罪去，儼至，發隱禁奸，號良二千石。

translations.literal: Advanced to Prefect of Pu Prefecture, where households and produce were abundant yet lawsuits had accumulated for years without settlement and previous prefects in succession left under charge of guilt; when Yan arrived he exposed hidden wrongs and forbade wickedness, and was called an excellent two-thousand-dan official.
translations.idiomatic: Made prefect of Pu, a rich and populous commandery where lawsuits had piled up for years and one magistrate after another had fled in disgrace, he rooted out concealed abuses and suppressed wrongdoing until men hailed him a model prefect.

sentences.zh: 永隆二年，以老致仕。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonglong he retired due to old age.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Yonglong he retired on account of age.

sentences.zh: 未幾，復召為太僕卿，以父諱辭官，徙太子右衛副率。

translations.literal: Before long he was again summoned as Minister of the Imperial Stud; he declined office on account of his father's name taboo and was moved to Deputy Commander of the Right Guard of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was recalled as minister of the imperial stud, but declined because the title violated his father's name and accepted instead the post of deputy commander of the heir apparent's right guard.

sentences.zh: 中宗在東宮，儼數爭過失，不見用。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was in the Eastern Palace, Yan repeatedly remonstrated over faults but was not heeded.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was crown prince, Yan repeatedly challenged his failings and was ignored.

sentences.zh: 自以總調護，不應諫。

translations.literal: He considered himself charged with overall supervision and ought to remonstrate.
translations.idiomatic: Believing he bore the chief duty of guiding the heir, he felt bound to speak plainly.

sentences.zh: 於是田遊岩興處士為洗馬，太子所尊禮，儼詒書責之曰：「太子年鼎盛，聖道有所未盡，足下受調護之寄，居責言之地，唯唯悠悠，不出一談。

translations.literal: Thereupon Tian Youyan, a hermit, became Wash-Horse and was honored and respected by the Heir Apparent; Yan sent a reproachful letter saying: "The Heir Apparent is in the prime of life; the sage way is not yet fully realized; you have received the charge of tutelage and hold the place of frank speech, yet you are evasive and indifferent and offer not one word of counsel.
translations.idiomatic: Then the recluse Tian Youyan was made wash-horse and treated with honor by the crown prince. Yan wrote to rebuke him: "The heir is young and the Way not yet complete. You were entrusted with his guidance and hold an office meant for plain speech, yet you drift along in silence.

sentences.zh: 向使不餐王粟，僕何敢議？

translations.literal: If in the past you had not eaten the king's grain, how would I dare to criticize?
translations.idiomatic: Had you never taken the court's stipend, I would not dare reproach you.

sentences.zh: 今祿及親矣，尚何酬塞？」

translations.literal: Now the stipend reaches your parents—what repayment is still owed?"
translations.idiomatic: Now your salary feeds your family—what debt to the throne remains unpaid?

sentences.zh: 遊岩愧不能答。

translations.literal: Youyan was ashamed and could not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Youyan was shamed into silence."

sentences.zh: 儼尋徙右衛大將軍，封義興縣子，以太子詹事致仕。

translations.literal: Yan was soon transferred to Right Guard Grand General, enfeoffed as Viscount of Yixing, and retired as Supervisor of the Heir Apparent's Household.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was soon made right guard grand general, created viscount of Yixing, and retired from the post of supervisor of the heir apparent's household.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十八。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died at seventy-eight.

sentences.zh: 中宗立，以舊恩贈禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was established, for old grace he was posthumously appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongzong took the throne, Yan was posthumously made minister of rites in remembrance of long service.

sentences.zh: 韋弘機韋弘機，京兆萬年人。

translations.literal: Wei Hongji—Wei Hongji, a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.
translations.idiomatic: Wei Hongji was a native of Wannian in Jingzhao.

sentences.zh: 祖元禮，隋浙州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yuanli was Prefect of Zhe Prefecture in Sui.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yuanli had been prefect of Zhe under the Sui.

sentences.zh: 弘機仕貞觀時為左千牛胄曹參軍，使西突厥，冊拜同俄設為可汗。

translations.literal: Hongji served in Zhenguan as Left Thousand-Ox Armor Army Adjutant; sent to the Western Turks, he enfeoffed Tong'e She as khan.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenguan era Hongji served as adjutant of the Left Thousand-Ox Armor Army and, sent to the Western Turks, invested Tong'e She as khan.

sentences.zh: 會石國叛，道梗，三年不得歸。

translations.literal: When the Shi Kingdom rebelled the roads were blocked, and for three years he could not return.
translations.idiomatic: A revolt in the Shi Kingdom cut the routes home, and he was stranded abroad for three years.

sentences.zh: 裂裾錄所過諸國風俗、物產，為《西征記》。

translations.literal: He tore his robe hem to record the customs and products of the countries he passed through and composed the Record of the Western Expedition.
translations.idiomatic: He tore strips from his robe to note the customs and products of every land he crossed and compiled the Record of the Western Expedition.

sentences.zh: 比還，太宗問外國事，即上其書。

translations.literal: When he returned Emperor Taizong asked about foreign affairs, and he immediately submitted his book.
translations.idiomatic: On his return Taizong questioned him about foreign lands, and he at once presented the work.

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，擢朝散大夫。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and promoted him to Gentleman for Dispersing Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was delighted and made him a gentleman for dispersing affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷殿中監。

translations.literal: He rose in succession to Vice Director of Palace Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He later rose to vice director of palace affairs.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，為檀州刺史，以邊人陋僻，不知文儒貴，乃脩學官，畫孔子、七十二子、漢晉名儒象，自為贊，敦勸生徒，繇是大化。

translations.literal: In Xianqing he was Prefect of Tan Prefecture; the border people were crude and remote and did not know the worth of literary scholars, so he repaired the academy, painted images of Confucius, the seventy-two disciples, and famous scholars of Han and Jin, wrote eulogies himself, and earnestly urged the students—whereby a great transformation took place.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Tan in the Xianqing era he found frontier folk ignorant of learning. He rebuilt the school, painted Confucius, the seventy-two disciples, and eminent Han and Jin scholars, wrote the inscriptions himself, and pressed the students until the region was transformed.

sentences.zh: 契苾何力討高麗。

translations.literal: Qibi Heli campaigned against Goguryeo.
