translations.idiomatic: Qibi Heli marched against Goguryeo.

sentences.zh: 次灤水，會暴漲，師留三日。

translations.literal: At Luanshui they met a sudden flood, and the army halted three days.
translations.idiomatic: At the Luanshui the army was stopped three days by a sudden flood.

sentences.zh: 弘機輸給資糧，軍無饑，高宗善之，擢司農少卿，主東都營田苑。

translations.literal: Hongji supplied provisions; the army suffered no hunger; Emperor Gaozong approved and promoted him to Vice Minister of Agriculture, putting him in charge of the Eastern Capital farm gardens.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji kept the supplies flowing so the troops did not go hungry. Gaozong praised him, made him vice minister of agriculture, and set him over the Eastern Capital farms and parks.

sentences.zh: 宦者犯法，杖乃奏，帝嗟賞，賜絹五十匹，曰：「後有犯，治之，毋奏。」

translations.literal: When a eunuch violated the law he was beaten and only then submitted a memorial; the Emperor sighed in approval, bestowed fifty bolts of silk, and said: "Later if there are violations, punish them—do not submit memorials."
translations.idiomatic: After he had a lawbreaking eunuch beaten and then reported the case, the emperor sighed his approval, gave him fifty bolts of silk, and said: "Next time simply punish offenders—no need to memorialize me.

sentences.zh: 遷司農卿。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was then promoted to minister of agriculture."

sentences.zh: 太子弘薨，詔蒲州刺史李沖寂治陵，成而玄堂阨，不容終具，將更為之。

translations.literal: When Heir Apparent Hong died, an edict had Pu Prefect Li Chongji oversee the mausoleum; when it was finished the inner chamber was cramped and could not accommodate the full burial furnishings, and they were about to rebuild.
translations.idiomatic: After Crown Prince Hong died, Pu prefect Li Chongji was ordered to build the tomb. When the work was done the burial chamber proved too small for the full funeral gear, and a rebuild was planned.

sentences.zh: 役者過期不遣，眾怨，夜燒營去。

translations.literal: The laborers, overdue and not dismissed, grew resentful; by night they burned the camp and left.
translations.idiomatic: The workers, kept past their term, mutinied and burned the camp one night before fleeing.

sentences.zh: 帝詔弘機嗣作，弘機令開隧左右為四便房，撙制禮物，裁工程，不多改作，如期而辦。

translations.literal: The Emperor ordered Hongji to continue the work; Hongji had the tunnel opened left and right into four side chambers, restrained the ceremonial objects, trimmed the engineering, made few alterations, and finished on schedule.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong put Hongji in charge. He widened the tunnel with four side chambers, scaled back the ritual furnishings and the construction, changed little else, and finished on time.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗言：「兩都，我東西宅，然因隋宮室日仆不完，朕將更作，奈財用何？」

translations.literal: The Emperor once said: "The two capitals are my east and west homes, yet because the Sui palace halls daily collapse and remain incomplete, I wish to rebuild—what of financial resources?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once remarked: "Chang'an and Luoyang are my two homes, but the old Sui palaces crumble daily. I want to rebuild—where will the money come from?

sentences.zh: 弘機即言：「臣任司農十年，省惜常費，積三十萬緡，以治宮室，可不勞而成。」

translations.literal: Hongji immediately said: "I have held the Ministry of Agriculture for ten years, saved routine expenses, and accumulated three hundred thousand strings of cash—to repair the palace halls can be done without toil."
translations.idiomatic: Hongji answered at once: "In ten years as minister of agriculture I have pared routine costs and saved three hundred thousand strings of cash. With that the work can be done without strain."

sentences.zh: 帝大悅，詔兼將作、少府二官，督營繕。

translations.literal: The Emperor was greatly pleased and ordered him to hold concurrently the posts of Master of Construction and Palace Treasures and to supervise construction and repair.
translations.idiomatic: Delighted, the emperor made him concurrently master of construction and palace treasures and put him in charge of the rebuilding."

sentences.zh: 初作宿羽、高山等宮，徙洛中橋于長夏門，廢利涉橋，人便之。

translations.literal: Initially he built the Suyu, Gaoshan, and other palaces; moved the Luoyang bridge to Changxia Gate; abolished Lishi Bridge; the people found it convenient.
translations.idiomatic: He first built Suyu, Gaoshan, and other palaces, moved the Luoyang bridge to Changxia Gate, and removed Lishi Bridge—all to the people's benefit.

sentences.zh: 天子乃登洛北絕岸，延眺良久，歎其美，詔即其地營宮，所謂上陽者。

translations.literal: The Son of Heaven then ascended the sheer north bank of the Luo, gazed far for a long time, sighed at its beauty, and ordered a palace built on that very spot—the one called Shangyang.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor climbed the towering north bank of the Luo River, lingered long in contemplation, and sighing at the view commanded a palace there—the palace known as Shangyang.

sentences.zh: 尚書左僕射劉仁軌謂侍御史狄仁傑曰：「古天子陂池臺榭皆深宮復禁，不欲百姓見之，恐傷其心。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs Liu Ren'gui said to Investigating Censor Di Renjie: "In antiquity the ponds, pools, terraces, and pavilions of the Son of Heaven were all deep within the palace, doubly walled and barred; he did not wish the common people to see them, fearing it would wound their hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Left vice director Liu Ren'gui told investigating censor Di Renjie: "Ancient sovereigns kept their lakes, pools, terraces, and pavilions locked within the inner palace, hidden from common sight lest the spectacle break the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 而今列岸謻廊亙王城外，豈愛君哉？」

translations.literal: Yet now ranked galleries and lofty arcades stretch across outside the royal city—is this love for the sovereign?"
translations.idiomatic: Now galleries line the banks and long covered walks run beyond the royal city walls—is that what love of the ruler looks like?"

sentences.zh: 弘機猥曰：「天下有道，百官奉職，任輔弼者，則思獻替事。

translations.literal: Hongji rudely said: "When the realm has the Way, the hundred officials fulfill their duties; those charged as aides and counselors then think of offering advice and remedies.
translations.idiomatic: Hongji answered bluntly: "When the realm is well governed every official keeps his post, and those who serve as counselors owe frank counsel.

sentences.zh: 我乃府藏臣，守官而已。」

translations.literal: I am merely a granary and treasury official—I simply keep my post, that is all."
translations.idiomatic: I am only a steward of storehouses and treasuries. I do my job and nothing more."

sentences.zh: 仁傑非之。

translations.literal: Renjie disapproved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Renjie rejected the reply.

sentences.zh: 俄坐家人犯盜，劾免官。

translations.literal: Soon, on account of a family member's theft, he was impeached and dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Before long a theft by a member of his household was charged against him and he was removed from office.

sentences.zh: 初，東都方士朱欽遂為武后所寵，奸贓狼藉。

translations.literal: Initially, the Taoist adept Zhu Qinsui of the Eastern Capital was favored by Empress Wu; his corruption was notorious.
translations.idiomatic: At first the Eastern Capital adept Zhu Qinsui enjoyed Empress Wu's favor, and his bribery and theft were notorious.

sentences.zh: 弘機白：「欽遂假中宮驅策，依倚形勢，虧紊皇明，為禍亂之漸。」

translations.literal: Hongji reported: "Qinsui abuses the power of the inner palace as his whip, relies on his backing, undermines and confounds imperial clarity, and is the beginning of calamity and disorder."
translations.idiomatic: Hongji memorialized: "Qinsui wields the empress's power as a lash, leans on her favor, corrupts the court, and opens the way to disaster."

sentences.zh: 帝遣中使慰諭，敕毋漏言，逐欽遂于邊，后恨之。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent a palace envoy to comfort and instruct him, ordered that the matter not be leaked, and banished Qinsui to the frontier; the Empress resented this.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a palace envoy to soothe Hongji, forbade him to speak of the affair, and banished Qinsui to the borderlands; the empress never forgave it.

sentences.zh: 永淳中，帝幸東都，至芳桂宮，召弘機使白衣檢校園苑，將復任之，為后犄而止。

translations.literal: In the Yongchun era, the Emperor visited the Eastern Capital, reached Fanggui Palace, summoned Hongji in plain clothes to serve as acting inspector of the parks, and was about to restore him to office, but was blocked by the Empress's obstruction.
translations.idiomatic: During Yongchun the emperor came to Luoyang and reached Fanggui Palace. He recalled Hongji in plain dress to oversee the parks and was ready to restore him, but the empress blocked the appointment.

sentences.zh: 終檢校司農少卿事。

translations.literal: In the end he served as acting Vice Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He ended his career as acting vice minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 孫 岳子孫岳子、景駿。

translations.literal: Grandson Yuezi and Jingjun.
translations.idiomatic: His grandsons were Yuezi and Jingjun.

sentences.zh: 景駿別傳。

translations.literal: Jingjun has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 岳子，武后時為汝州司馬，以辨治稱。

translations.literal: Yuezi, during Empress Wu's time served as Vice Commandant of Ru Prefecture, famed for discernment in governance.
translations.idiomatic: Under Empress Wu, Yuezi was vice commandant of Ru Prefecture and won fame for clear, capable administration.

sentences.zh: 召授尚舍奉禦，入見，后賞其能，曰：「卿家事，朕悉知之。」

translations.literal: Summoned and appointed Palace Provision Attendant; on entering audience the Empress praised his ability and said: "Your family affairs—I know them all thoroughly."
translations.idiomatic: Called to court and made palace provision attendant, he was praised by the empress, who said: "I know your family's affairs down to the last detail."

sentences.zh: 因問舊故，至家人皆不忘。

translations.literal: She then asked about old acquaintances, even to family members—none forgotten.
translations.idiomatic: She questioned him about old ties, even naming relatives, and forgot nothing.

sentences.zh: 出為太原令，以不習武固辭，忤旨，下遷宋州長史。

translations.literal: Sent out as Magistrate of Taiyuan; he firmly declined on grounds of being unskilled in military matters, offended the imperial will, and was demoted to Chief Secretary of Song Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Sent out as magistrate of Taiyuan, he refused on the ground that he knew nothing of military affairs, drew imperial displeasure, and was demoted to chief secretary of Song Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 歷廬、海等州刺史，皆著風跡，恩嚴兩施。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Prefect of Lu, Hai, and other prefectures; everywhere he left a mark of conduct, blending kindness and severity.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as prefect of Lu, Hai, and other prefectures, leaving a record of firm but fair rule wherever he went.

sentences.zh: 睿宗立，召為殿中少監，恩遇尤異。

translations.literal: When Ruizong took the throne, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Palace Administration and received exceptionally favored treatment.
translations.idiomatic: When Ruizong came to the throne Yuezi was recalled as vice director of the palace administration and treated with unusual favor.

sentences.zh: 竇懷貞等誅，而嶽子舊與經過，為薑晈所劾，貶渠州別駕。

translations.literal: When Dou Huaizhen and others were executed, Yuezi had old associations with them and was impeached by Jiang Jiao, demoted to Vice Prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: After Dou Huaizhen and his faction were put to death, Yuezi's old ties with them were exposed by Jiang Jiao's impeachment, and he was demoted to vice prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 起授陝州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: Restored and appointed Prefect of Shan Prefecture; he died.
translations.idiomatic: Later restored, he was made prefect of Shan Prefecture and died in office.

sentences.zh: 孫皋，別有傳。

translations.literal: Sun Gao has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Sun Gao is treated in a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 姜師度姜師度，魏州魏人。

translations.literal: Jiang Shidu—Jiang Shidu, a native of Wei in Weizhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Shidu was a native of Wei in Weizhou.

sentences.zh: 擢明經，調丹陵尉、龍崗令，有清白稱。

translations.literal: Raised through the Mingjing examination, appointed Captain of Danling and Magistrate of Longgang; he had a reputation for integrity.
translations.idiomatic: Passed through the Mingjing examination and served as captain of Danling and magistrate of Longgang, earning a name for spotless conduct.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，試為易州刺史、河北道巡察，兼支度營田使。

translations.literal: Early in Shenlong, he was given a provisional appointment as Prefect of Yi Prefecture and Inspector of the Hebei Circuit, concurrently Commissioner for Provisioning and Military Farms.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Shenlong era he was provisionally made prefect of Yi, inspector of the Hebei circuit, and commissioner for provisioning and military farms.

sentences.zh: 好興作，始廝溝於薊門，以限奚、契丹，循魏武帝故跡，並海鑿平虜渠，以通餉路，罷海運，省功多。

translations.literal: He loved public works. He first dug a barrier trench at Ji's Gate to restrain the Xi and Khitan, followed the old traces of Emperor Wu of Wei, and along the coast excavated the Pinglu Canal to open supply routes, abolishing sea transport and saving much labor.
translations.idiomatic: He loved grand projects. At Ji's Gate he opened a defensive trench against the Xi and Khitan, retraced Emperor Wu of Wei's old route, and cut the Pinglu Canal along the coast to feed the armies by land, ending sea transport and saving enormous labor.

sentences.zh: 遷司農卿。

translations.literal: Transferred to Minister of Agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of agriculture.

sentences.zh: 出為陝州刺史。

translations.literal: Sent out as Prefect of Shan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as prefect of Shan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太原倉水陸運所湊，轉屬諸河，師度使依高為廥，而注米於舟，以故人不勞。

translations.literal: The Taiyuan granary was a convergence point for water and land transport, transferring goods to various rivers. Shidu had granaries built on high ground and poured rice into boats, so the people were not wearied.
translations.idiomatic: The Taiyuan depot gathered both river and road traffic bound for many waterways. Shidu built elevated granaries and poured grain straight into boats, sparing the people heavy labor.

sentences.zh: 拜太子詹事。

translations.literal: Appointed Grand Preceptor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He was made grand preceptor of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 玄宗徙營州治柳城，拜營田支度脩築使。

translations.literal: When Xuanzong moved Ying Prefecture's seat to Liucheng, Shidu was appointed Commissioner for Military Farms, Provisioning, and Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Xuanzong shifted the seat of Ying Prefecture to Liucheng, Shidu was appointed commissioner for military farms, provisioning, and construction.

sentences.zh: 進為河中尹。

translations.literal: Promoted to Governor of Hezhong.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to governor of Hezhong.

sentences.zh: 安邑鹽池涸廢，師度大發卒，洫引其流，置鹽屯，公私收利不貲。

translations.literal: The Anyi salt ponds had dried up and fallen into disuse. Shidu conscripted a huge force of laborers, irrigated and drew their flow, established salt colonies, and public and private profits were immeasurable.
translations.idiomatic: The Anyi salt flats had dried up and gone to waste. Shidu mobilized a vast labor force, reopened the channels, and established salt colonies until public and private profit alike became incalculable.

sentences.zh: 徙同州刺史。

translations.literal: Transferred to Prefect of Tong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to prefect of Tong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 又派洛灌朝邑、河西二縣，閼河以灌通靈陂，收棄地二千頃為上田，置十餘屯。

translations.literal: He also diverted the Luo to irrigate Chaoyi and Hexi counties, blocked the river to fill the Tongling reservoir, reclaimed two thousand qing of abandoned land as top-grade fields, and established more than ten colonies.
translations.idiomatic: He also diverted the Luo to water Chaoyi and Hexi, dammed the stream to fill Tongling reservoir, turned two thousand qing of waste land into prime fields, and set up more than ten military colonies.

sentences.zh: 帝幸長春宮，嘉其功，下詔褒美，加金紫光祿大夫，賜帛三百匹。

translations.literal: The Emperor visited Changchun Palace, praised his achievements, issued an edict of commendation, added the rank of Grand Master with Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon, and bestowed three hundred bolts of silk.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor visited Changchun Palace he praised the work, issued a commendatory edict, raised Shidu to grand master with gold seal and purple ribbon, and gave him three hundred bolts of silk.

sentences.zh: 進將作大匠。

translations.literal: Promoted to Master of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to master of palace construction.

sentences.zh: 左拾遺劉彤建榷天下鹽鐵利內之官，免貧民賦，詔戶部侍郎強循與師度並假御史中丞，會諸道按察使議所以榷之之法，俄為議者沮，閣不行。

translations.literal: Remonstrance Official Liu Tong proposed monopolizing under government the profits of salt and iron throughout the realm and exempting the poor from levies. An edict had Vice Minister of Revenue Qiang Xun and Shidu both provisionally appointed as Vice Imperial Censors, summoning the circuit inspectors to discuss methods of monopoly, but soon opponents blocked it and the matter was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance official Liu Tong urged that salt and iron profits nationwide be brought under state control and the poor relieved of tax. The court ordered vice minister of revenue Qiang Xun and Shidu, both acting as vice imperial censors, to meet the circuit inspectors and draft a monopoly scheme, but critics soon blocked it and the plan died.

sentences.zh: 卒，年七十餘。

translations.literal: He died at age seventy-odd.
translations.idiomatic: He died in his seventies.

sentences.zh: 師度喜渠漕，所至繇役紛紜，不能皆便，然所就必為後世利。

translations.literal: Shidu delighted in canals and water transport; wherever he went corvée labor was complex and not everyone was benefited, yet what he completed always profited later generations.
translations.idiomatic: Shidu loved canals and grain transport. His projects always meant heavy corvée and not every community gained at once, yet what he finished proved a lasting benefit.

sentences.zh: 是時太史令傅孝忠以知星顯，時為語曰：「孝忠知仰天，師度知相地。」

translations.literal: At the time Grand Astrologer Fu Xiaozhong was famed for knowing the stars, and a saying of the day ran: "Xiaozhong knows to look heavenward; Shidu knows to read the earth."
translations.idiomatic: Grand astrologer Fu Xiaozhong was then famous for reading the heavens, and people said: "Xiaozhong reads the sky; Shidu reads the land."

sentences.zh: 嘲所嗜也。

translations.literal: This mocked their obsessions.
translations.idiomatic: The jingle mocked their respective passions.

sentences.zh: 附 強循強循字季先，鳳州人。

translations.literal: Appendix: Qiang Xun—Qiang Xun, courtesy name Jixian, a native of Feng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Qiang Xun, whose courtesy name was Jixian, came from Feng Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 仕累雍州司士參軍。

translations.literal: Through office he rose to Army Aide of the Bureau of Administration in Yong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In service he rose to army aide in the Yongzhou bureau of administration.

sentences.zh: 華原無泉，人畜多暍死。

translations.literal: Huayuan had no springs; men and livestock often died of heatstroke.
translations.idiomatic: Huayuan had no springs, and men and beasts often died of heat and thirst.

sentences.zh: 循教人渠水以浸田，一方利之，號強公渠。

translations.literal: Xun taught the people to channel water to irrigate fields; the whole region benefited, and it was called Lord Qiang's Canal.
translations.idiomatic: Xun showed the people how to bring canal water to the fields. The whole district prospered, and the channel was named Lord Qiang's Canal.

sentences.zh: 詔書褒予甚厚。

translations.literal: An imperial edict praised and rewarded him very generously.
translations.idiomatic: An imperial edict praised him and rewarded him handsomely.

sentences.zh: 歷大理少卿、太子右庶子。

translations.literal: He served in succession as Vice Minister of Justice and Right Vice Grand Master of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as vice minister of justice and right vice grand master of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 為政辦給，不為威嚴，遇人盡信不疑，然當時恨其少文云。

translations.literal: In governing he was efficient and provided for needs, not given to severity; in dealing with people he trusted completely without suspicion, yet at the time people regretted his lack of refinement.
translations.idiomatic: As an administrator he was brisk and practical rather than stern, trusting everyone without question; contemporaries regretted only that he lacked polish.

sentences.zh: 張知謇張知謇，子匪躬，幽州方城人，徙家岐。

translations.literal: Zhang Zhijian—Zhang Zhijian, courtesy name Feigong, a native of Fangcheng in You Prefecture; the family moved to Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhijian, courtesy name Feigong, came from Fangcheng in You Prefecture; his family later settled in Qi.

sentences.zh: 兄弟五人，知玄、知晦、知泰、知默，皆明經高第，曉吏治，清介有守，公卿爭為引重。

translations.literal: Five brothers—Zhixuan, Zhihui, Zhita, and Zhim— all passed the Mingjing with high marks, understood administration, were upright and firm in principle, and the high ministers competed to recommend them.
translations.idiomatic: Five brothers—Zhixuan, Zhihui, Zhita, and Zhim—all passed the Mingjing with high honors, knew administration, and were upright men of principle whom the great ministers vied to advance.

sentences.zh: 調露時，知謇監察御史裏行，知默左臺侍御史。

translations.literal: In the Tiaolu era, Zhijian served as Provisional Investigating Censor; Zhim served as Regular Attendant Censor of the Left Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: During Tiaolu, Zhijian was a provisional investigating censor and Zhim a regular attendant censor of the left bureau.

sentences.zh: 知謇歷十一州刺史，所蒞有威嚴，武后降璽書存問。

translations.literal: Zhijian served eleven prefectures in succession as prefect; wherever he went he had awe-inspiring dignity; Empress Wu sent imperial sealed letters of inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian governed eleven prefectures in succession with commanding authority, and Empress Wu sent him sealed letters of inquiry.

sentences.zh: 萬歲通天中，自德州刺史入計，后奇其貌，詔工圖之，稱其兄弟容而才，謂之兩絕。

translations.literal: In the Wansui Tongtian era, coming from De Prefecture as prefect to render the annual account, the Empress found his appearance remarkable, ordered artists to paint him, praised the brothers' looks and talent, and called them doubly preeminent.
translations.idiomatic: During Wansui Tongtian he came from De Prefecture to present the annual accounts. The empress was struck by his looks, had him painted, praised the brothers' appearance and ability together, and called them unmatched in both.

sentences.zh: 又門皆列戟，白雀巢其廷，后數寵賜。

translations.literal: Moreover their gates all displayed halberds; white magpies nested in their courtyards; the Empress repeatedly bestowed favors.
translations.idiomatic: Halberds stood at every gate, white magpies nested in their courtyards, and the empress showered them with favor.

sentences.zh: 知泰歷益州長史、中臺左丞、兵部侍郎，封陳留縣公。

translations.literal: Zhita served in succession as Chief Secretary of Yi Prefecture, Left Vice Director of the Central Secretariat, and Vice Minister of War; he was enfeoffed as Duke of Chenliu County.
translations.idiomatic: Zhita rose through chief secretary of Yi, left vice director of the central secretariat, and vice minister of war, and was created duke of Chenliu County.

sentences.zh: 中宗在房州，禁察苛嚴。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong was at Fang Prefecture, surveillance and restrictions were harsh and severe.
translations.idiomatic: While Zhongzong was confined at Fang Prefecture, surveillance was merciless.

sentences.zh: 知謇與董玄質、崔敬嗣繼為刺史，供儗保戴不少弛。

translations.literal: Zhijian, Dong Xuanzhi, and Cui Jingsi served in succession as prefects; their provisions and protective care never slackened.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian, Dong Xuanzhi, and Cui Jingsi served there in turn as prefects, and none of them eased in supplying or protecting him.

sentences.zh: 帝復位，拜知謇左衛將軍，加雲麾將軍，封范陽郡公；

translations.literal: When the Emperor restored his throne, Zhijian was appointed General of the Left Guards, given the additional title of General of Cloud Banners, and enfeoffed as Duke of Fanyang Commandery;
translations.idiomatic: After the emperor regained the throne, Zhijian was made general of the left guards, given the additional title of cloud-banner general, and created duke of Fanyang Commandery;

sentences.zh: 知泰御史臺大夫，加銀青光祿大夫，封漁陽郡公。

translations.literal: Zhita was made Chief Imperial Censor, given the additional rank of Grand Master with Silver Seal and Purple Ribbon, and enfeoffed as Duke of Yuyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Zhita was made chief imperial censor, given the rank of grand master with silver seal and purple ribbon, and created duke of Yuyang Commandery.

sentences.zh: 伯仲華首同貴，時以為榮。

translations.literal: Elder and younger among the flower of the land shared equal eminence; the age regarded it as glorious.
translations.idiomatic: Two brothers stood at the summit of honor together, and their contemporaries took it as a family glory.

sentences.zh: 知泰忤武三思，故出為并州刺史、天兵軍使。

translations.literal: Zhita offended Wu Sansi and was therefore sent out as Prefect of Bing Prefecture and Commissioner of the Tianbing Army.
translations.idiomatic: Zhita crossed Wu Sansi and was sent out as prefect of Bing and commissioner of the Tianbing army.

sentences.zh: 終魏州刺史，諡曰定。

translations.literal: He ended as Prefect of Wei Prefecture; posthumous name Ding.
translations.idiomatic: He ended as prefect of Wei Prefecture and received the posthumous name Ding.

sentences.zh: 知謇歷東都副留守、左右羽林大將軍、同華州刺史，大理卿致仕。

translations.literal: Zhijian served as Eastern Capital Vice Custodian, Grand General of the Left and Right Feathered Forest Armies, and Prefect of Tong and Hua; he retired as Chief Justice of the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: Zhijian served as Luoyang vice custodian, grand general of the left and right feathered forest armies, and prefect of Tong and Hua, then retired as chief justice of the court of judicial review.

sentences.zh: 年八十，開元時卒。

translations.literal: At age eighty he died in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: He died at eighty during the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 知謇敏且亮，惡請謁求進，士或不才冒位，視之若仇。

translations.literal: Zhijian was quick and bright; he hated petitioning and seeking advancement; when scholars of no talent usurped posts, he regarded them as enemies.
translations.idiomatic: Quick and sharp of mind, Zhijian despised favor-seeking and treated unworthy men who clawed their way into office as enemies.

sentences.zh: 每敕子孫「經不明不得舉」，家法可稱云。

translations.literal: He repeatedly admonished his descendants: "If the classics are not mastered, you may not be recommended,"—family discipline worthy of praise.
translations.idiomatic: He often warned his descendants, "No one who has not mastered the classics may be recommended,"—a household rule worth remembering.

sentences.zh: 武后革命，知泰奏置東都諸關十七所，譏斂出入。

translations.literal: When Empress Wu changed the dynasty, Zhita memorialized to establish seventeen passes around the Eastern Capital to levy tolls on entry and exit.
translations.idiomatic: After Empress Wu's takeover Zhita proposed seventeen checkpoints around Luoyang to tax goods going in and out.

sentences.zh: 百姓驚駭，樵米踴貴，卒罷不用，議者羞薄之。

translations.literal: The common people were alarmed; firewood and rice prices soared; in the end it was abolished and unused; commentators held it in shame and contempt.
translations.idiomatic: The people panicked, firewood and grain prices shot up, and the scheme was finally abandoned; critics treated it as a disgrace.

sentences.zh: 知默與監察御史王守慎、來俊臣、周興掌詔獄，數陷大臣。

translations.literal: Zhim together with Investigating Censor Wang Shouzhen, Lai Junchen, and Zhou Xing supervised imperial prison cases, repeatedly entrapping high ministers.
translations.idiomatic: Zhim joined investigating censor Wang Shouzhen, Lai Junchen, and Zhou Xing in running the empress's prison network and repeatedly framed high ministers.

sentences.zh: 守慎雖其甥，惡鞫引之暴，不得去，請度為浮屠，后許之。

translations.literal: Though Shouzhen was his nephew, he hated the brutality of forced confessions; unable to leave, he requested to become a Buddhist monk; the Empress granted it.
translations.idiomatic: Shouzhen was his nephew, yet he loathed the violence of forced confessions; unable to escape, he asked to become a monk, and the empress allowed it.

sentences.zh: 而知默卒陷酷吏，子孫禁錮，為張氏羞。

translations.literal: But Zhim ultimately fell in with the cruel officials; his descendants were banned from office—a disgrace to the Zhang clan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhim himself sank into the company of the cruel officials; his descendants were barred from office, a stain on the Zhang name.

sentences.zh: 知玄子景升，知泰子景佚，開元中皆顯官。

translations.literal: Zhixuan's son Jingsheng and Zhita's son Jingyi both became prominent officials in the Kaiyuan era.
translations.idiomatic: Zhixuan's son Jingsheng and Zhita's son Jingyi both rose to high office in the Kaiyuan era.
